stories.background:
Gowda's wife's complaint led to an FIR and six arrests. The Karnataka government transferred the case to the CBI in 2019. The CBI said Gowda had refused to withdraw from the 2016 Zilla Panchayat election, which led to enmity with Kulkarni.

Kulkarni was arrested by the CBI in November 2020 and got Supreme Court bail in August 2021. The court cancelled that bail in June 2025 after finding material indicating he had tried to influence prosecution witnesses. He was Minister of State for Mines and Geology in the first Siddaramaiah Cabinet and won the Dharwad seat in 2023.
stories.whyItMatters: Kulkarni and the co-convicts return to custody while their appeals are heard. The ruling also states that long delays in hearing appeals are not by themselves grounds to suspend life sentences in grave offences.

body: The US Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday authorised SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million satellites carrying AI chips as orbital data centres, under an initiative called Starmind.

The Verge reported that the FCC announced the approval, which covers satellites equipped with AI chips and is part of the Elon Musk-owned company's plan. The Guardian, citing the FCC statement, described the satellites as orbital compute modules built by SpaceX that would process data in space.

According to The Guardian, the authorisation requires SpaceX to deploy 100,000 of the satellites no later than November 2035. The Guardian also reported that the FCC called the decision a step to "support America's booming super intelligence economy".

The Guardian reported that it is the first such authorisation in US history. The Verge said it is the first approval of its kind the agency has granted, as several other companies, including Google and Blue Origin, also pursue the idea of putting AI data centres in space.
Ars Technica reported that the constellation would increase the number of satellites in orbit by roughly 50-fold.

stories.headline: US Army detonates entire lead azide stockpile at Iowa plant as residents voice health fears
stories.dek: The controlled blast destroyed the country's remaining supply of the unstable explosive; NASA flew three aircraft to track the plume, and residents were told to stay indoors.
stories.summary: The US Army detonated its entire stockpile of lead azide, nearly five tonnes, at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant on Wednesday, saying the material had become too unstable to store. Residents had raised concerns about lead dust, and NASA monitored the plume.
body: The US Army detonated the country's entire stockpile of lead azide, nearly five tonnes of ageing explosive, at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown on Wednesday morning, saying the material had become too unstable to keep.

The Guardian put the amount at 9,700lb (4,400kg). The blast took place at about 10am Eastern time, according to the Guardian and Space.com. Middletown, in south-eastern Iowa, has about 400 residents. Smoke was visible from about a mile away, the Guardian reported.

The material was moved to the Iowa plant from bases around the country in 2009, DW reported. A March inspection found it had partly crystallised, which makes it sensitive to friction and cold and could set off a spontaneous explosion. Major General Eric Shirley, who leads the operation, said: "Inaction is no longer an option."
Rob Cekada, director of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, told reporters: "It's not a matter of if, it's a matter of when."

To limit lead dust, the Army built barriers around the bunkers and planned to use foam and water to trap particles. Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle said: "We don't believe that the public should be in a panic." He said the goal was to keep as much material as possible on the site.

Army projections cited by Reuters showed dust could settle up to 40 miles (64 km) south-west, reaching northern Missouri. STAT reported an Army analysis found a plume could travel up to 100 miles, affecting homes and 350 farms. Officials expected winds to carry the plume away from Burlington, a city of nearly 25,000.

Residents within 5 miles (8 km) were encouraged to evacuate. The Federal Emergency Management Agency advised people 5 to 20 miles away to stay indoors with windows closed. Space.com reported officials urged residents to stay indoors for 24 to 28 hours after the blast. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention activated an emergency response.

NASA sent a P-3 Orion, a Gulfstream III and a B200 aircraft, and used its TEMPO instrument on a commercial satellite, to collect atmospheric data. Administrator Jared Isaacman rejected comparisons to Chernobyl, saying there was no reactor and no fission products.

The detonation date changed three times after public objections. A federal appeals court cleared the plan on Monday after environmental groups sued. Farmer Jill Holler, who organised a protest, told Reuters: "I'm not opposed if this is the only safe option." She added that it had been "so mishandled that people are confused and don't trust anything they're saying."

President Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social that early reports showed the Army's mitigation efforts "far exceeded expectations". Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said on X that his department would stay on the ground to support the response and cleanup.

NASA deployed three aircraft and a satellite instrument to monitor the plume.

stories.headline: World records six straight days 2C above pre-industrial levels for first time
stories.dek: The streak is continuing, but scientists say it is too short to show the Paris Agreement's upper temperature limit has been breached.
stories.summary: Daily global surface temperature reached a record 2.24C above the pre-industrial baseline on Monday, the Guardian reported, the sixth straight day above 2C. The streak came days after COP31 ended in Turkey without a deal.
body: The world has recorded six consecutive days with global temperatures at least 2C above pre-industrial levels for the first time, the Guardian reported on Wednesday, adding that the streak is continuing.

Daily global surface temperature reached a record 2.24C above the baseline on Monday, according to the Guardian, which said it had learned of the figures. The newspaper said the streak is forecast to continue.

Scientists told the Guardian the run is too brief to mean the upper range of the Paris climate agreement target has been breached. They described it as an early indication of what is to come unless fossil fuel emissions are rapidly eliminated.

The record follows the end of the UN climate talks, known as COP31, in Turkey on Sunday. According to Reuters, the talks ended in collapse after the European Union and others rejected a final deal put forward by the conference presidents, Turkey and Australia. The objectors said the text was too weak to advance the fight against global warming.

Pope Leo expressed disappointment on Wednesday over the failed talks, Reuters reported. He urged the international community to take firm measures to protect the Earth and prevent the consequences of climate change.
keyFacts: Six consecutive days at 2C or more above pre-industrial levels, a first, the Guardian reported.

stories.background: The Paris climate agreement sets a long-term temperature target, with 2C as the upper end of its range. Scientists quoted by the Guardian said a short run of days above 2C does not amount to breaching that target.
stories.whyItMatters: Scientists told the Guardian the streak points to what lies ahead unless fossil fuel emissions are rapidly eliminated, while the COP31 talks produced no agreement.

stories.headline: US officials find no evidence Beijing directed Alice Huang to spy on Nvidia CEO
stories.dek: The Wall Street Journal reports that intelligence officials told congressional staff the evidence points to a personal relationship, though Alice Huang did contact China's spy agency.
stories.summary: US officials found no evidence that Alice Huang was directed by Beijing to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday. The assessment followed President Donald Trump's decision to clear the way for Huang's reinstatement.
body: US officials found no evidence that tech executive Alice Huang was directed by Beijing to spy on Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing people familiar with a classified briefing.

According to the Journal, officials from the CIA, FBI, Office of the Director of National Intelligence and National Security Agency briefed staff of congressional intelligence committees and chamber leaders.

The officials said Alice Huang had contacted China's spy agency during her relationship with Jensen Huang, the report said. They found no indication, however, that she had given it significant intelligence.

The available evidence pointed to an amorous relationship between the two, rather than a coordinated operation directed by Beijing, the Journal reported. It added that the assessment could change if new information emerges.

The briefing followed President Donald Trump's decision earlier this week to clear the way for Jensen Huang's reinstatement. Trump assured Nvidia that its chief executive did not pose a national-security threat.

The controversy centred on concerns over Alice Huang's alleged links to Chinese intelligence. It also touched on whether her relationship with Jensen Huang had any bearing on suspected diversions of Nvidia chips to China.

The New York Times published a profile of Alice Huang on Tuesday. It said she grew up in a small town built around a weapons factory and moved into finance and the technology industry, a path it said paralleled China's own rise.
The Journal's account is based on unnamed sources. The US agencies and Nvidia were not quoted in the material reviewed.

stories.headline: Tamil Nadu signs 78 MoUs worth ₹58,214 crore at Mahabalipuram investment conclave
stories.dek: Industries Minister S. Keerthana said the government will take responsibility for converting agreements into projects, citing a 74.1 percent conversion rate for earlier MoUs.
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu government signed 78 MoUs worth ₹58,214 crore, with the potential to create 65,786 jobs, at the second VETTRI investment conclave on Wednesday. Minister S. Keerthana said 83 of 112 earlier MoUs have reached land allotment or beyond.
body: The Tamil Nadu government signed 78 MoUs worth ₹58,214 crore, with the potential to create 65,786 jobs, at the second VETTRI Tamil Nadu Investment and Conversion Conclave on Wednesday, with Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay present.
ThePrint reported the event was held in Mahabalipuram; the state government's post on X and Times of India referred to Chennai. Fifty-eight of the 78 projects are greenfield, according to ThePrint.

The agreements include industrial and logistics parks worth ₹15,250 crore, renewable energy projects worth ₹11,142 crore, automotive projects worth ₹7,488 crore and critical engineering projects worth ₹6,463 crore. Others cover textiles, aerospace and defence, electronics and semiconductors.

WEG Industries has committed to a ₹2,000-crore facility in Dharmapuri that could create 3,000 jobs. Companies from Brazil, Germany, Finland, Singapore, South Korea, Sweden and the United States also signed MoUs.
The government said it has signed 190 MoUs since May, valued at ₹1.73 lakh crore, with the potential to create nearly two lakh jobs.

Industries Minister S. Keerthana said the government is focused on measurable conversion rather than announcements. She said 83 of 112 MoUs signed earlier, about 74.1 percent, have moved to land allotment and beyond in just over six months. She acknowledged that the remaining 25.9 percent have not reached that stage.

“Politicians usually tell you only where they are winning. I am telling you where the work is left,” Keerthana said. She added: “He has made conversion the government’s job, not the investor’s problem,” referring to Vijay.
ThePrint said the emphasis on conversion responds to earlier criticism that the government was claiming credit for commitments made under the previous DMK government.

Keerthana said industrial approvals are now mandated within 21 days, and that more than 25 reforms have been started through 23 Government Orders across 11 departments. Trade licences now last ten years instead of three, she said.

She said more than half the proposed projects are outside the state's four traditional industrial districts, and named Madurai and Trichy as future growth centres. Under the Vetri Magalir Thozhilmunaivor Membattu Thittam, 19 women entrepreneurs have received sanctions worth ₹13.26 crore, she said.
Ahead of the event, Times of India reported that the state plans plug-and-play industrial facilities at Gangaikondan and Tuticorin, and a digital land-allocation platform with 3D visualisation.

stories.headline: Karnataka drops Lalbagh land for tunnel road, surveys two alternative sites
stories.dek: Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said the Hebbal-Silk Board project's alignment will change, may cost more, and will not lead to higher tolls.
stories.summary: Karnataka has ruled out using Lalbagh Botanical Garden land for the Hebbal-Silk Board tunnel road, Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said on Wednesday. The government is surveying alternatives, and BJP MP Tejasvi Surya said his opposition to the project continues.
body: Karnataka has dropped plans to use Lalbagh Botanical Garden land for the Hebbal-Silk Board tunnel road and is surveying two alternative locations, Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said on Wednesday.

"The new alignment will be away from Lalbagh. We are undertaking a survey to assess the pros and cons of different locations. Final decisions are yet to be made," Gowda told reporters. He said the government had given people a promise to move the project outside the garden.

Deccan Herald reported that the original plan needed about six acres of Lalbagh for entry and exit ramps. It said Bengaluru Smart Infrastructure Ltd (B-SMILE) is scouting other land. One site is said to be KSRTC land near the corporation's headquarters in Shanthinagar. The other is said to be a vacant parcel at the Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Chest Diseases, near Nimhans. B-SMILE officials did not confirm either location. Hindustan Times reported that areas around Siddapura and Wilson Garden are among those considered. The sources differ on the sites, and the government has not announced them.

Gowda said the new route may raise the project cost because it will be longer than the original alignment. He said toll charges would not be increased. The state's contribution, he said, stays at ₹7,000 crore regardless of the contractor's quote.

Adani Enterprises emerged as the lowest bidder for two packages with a bid of ₹22,000 crore, according to South First. That is more than 90 percent above the government's estimated Total Concession Value of ₹17,800 crore. A committee headed by the chief secretary, with officials from the Finance and Public Works departments, is negotiating with the contractor to lower the price. Gowda said two rounds of talks have been held.
The revised alignment must return to the Cabinet for approval before a work order is issued, Gowda said.

Bengaluru South MP Tejasvi Surya, who led a protest in Lalbagh, called the decision "an initial victory for the citizens' movement". He said that changing the alignment "does not make the project scientific" and that his opposition will continue. He also challenged Gowda to a public debate on the project.

Hindustan Times reported that the Cabinet earlier this month resolved to exclude Lalbagh and withdrew the Karnataka Parks Conservation Amendment Bill.

stories.headline: Supreme Court inclined to stay HC order barring Kolkata civic poll notification
stories.dek: The bench asked Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to seek instructions by November 30 on the challenge to the expansion of Kolkata Municipal Corporation wards from 144 to 209.
stories.summary: The Supreme Court said on Wednesday it is inclined to stay a Calcutta High Court order that blocks notification of Kolkata Municipal Corporation elections. The High Court order stays in force until a challenge to ward delimitation is decided.
body: The Supreme Court on Wednesday said it is inclined to stay a Calcutta High Court order that bars the West Bengal State Election Commission from notifying Kolkata Municipal Corporation elections until a challenge to ward delimitation is decided.

A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana asked Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to seek instructions on the issue by November 30. Justice Bagchi said: "We shouldn't postpone pending elections unreasonably."

The bench said the writ petition pending before a single judge of the High Court would be directed to be transferred to its division bench. The division bench, it said, would pass a fresh, appropriate order.

The High Court's division bench had restrained the State Election Commission from issuing any notification calling the KMC election until the single-bench petition is disposed of. The restraint applies to polls based on the amended Schedule II of the KMC Act, notified in the gazette on September 11.

The petitioner, Dipu Das, is a former CPI-M councillor. He seeks a declaration that the exercise to fix the number of KMC wards is void, and the quashing of the September 11 notification. He alleges the delimitation used electoral rolls instead of actual population, leaving out a substantial number of residents.

Senior advocate Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya, for the petitioner, told the High Court that the state and its agencies had gerrymandered wards to give the ruling party an advantage based on past results. Advocate General S.N. Mitra argued that Section 601 of the KMC Act gives the state government ample power to alter the Schedules, with or without a recommendation from the Corporation.

A single judge, Justice Hiranmay Bhattacharyya, refused an interim stay on October 29. Mr. Das appealed, and the division bench of Justices Sabyasachi Bhattacharyya and Arjun Ray Mukherjee found he had made out a sufficiently strong prima facie case for interim protection. It described its observations as tentative for the final disposal of the petition.
The Supreme Court has not yet passed a formal order. The matter returns after the Centre's counsel reports on instructions by November 30.

The West Bengal government passed legislation in the Assembly on August 12 redrawing KMC wards and raising their number from 144 to 209. The gazette notification followed on September 11. After the BJP came to power in May 2026, the KMC board led by former Mayor Firhad Hakim and its councillors resigned, and the state appointed administrators.

Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari has several times said he prefers to hold civic elections in Kolkata and Howrah by the end of November or early December, according to The Hindu.

stories.headline: Supreme Court asks Centre, Delhi government for full reply on protest detentions
stories.dek: Delhi Police has told the court that a habeas corpus plea over Mamata Banerjee's alleged removal from the protest site is infructuous, saying no one was detained on October 10.
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday directed the Centre and the Delhi government to file a comprehensive response within 10 days to petitions over detentions during the October 10 protests in New Delhi. Delhi Police has said no one was arrested or detained that day.
body: The Supreme Court on Wednesday directed the Centre and the Delhi government to file a comprehensive response within 10 days to petitions alleging detentions, particularly of political leaders, during the October 10 anti-CEC protests in New Delhi.

A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana passed the order after Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati submitted that affidavits had been filed in only some of the petitions. The court asked petitioners to file any rejoinders within a week after the response.

Delhi Police has told the court that a habeas corpus petition by Trinamool Congress MP and lawyer Menaka Guruswamy has become infructuous. The petition concerned the alleged removal of former West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee from the protest site. Police said no one was arrested or detained during the October 10 protests.

The Hindu reported that the protest call was given by the CJP and some student organisations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, over alleged irregularities in the functioning of the Election Commission.

The Hindu also reported that the planned mass mobilisation at Jantar Mantar was thwarted after a security clampdown and the detention of more than 7,000 protesters. It said those held included CJP leader Abhijit Dipke, several opposition leaders and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee. That figure sits against the police statement to the court that no one was detained, and the sources do not reconcile the two.

In a special sitting on October 11, the court had said people gathering peacefully should not be illegally detained. It also asked the Centre to ensure that the Delhi Metro functions normally and that internet services are not disrupted, subject to law-and-order conditions.
Habeas corpus is a constitutional remedy used to protect individual liberty against unlawful detention or restraint.

stories.headline: Mumbai marks 18 years since 26/11 attacks, with parking curbs in south Mumbai
stories.dek: Traffic police have barred parking in parts of south Mumbai until 10 a.m. on Thursday for the memorial programme at the Police Commissioner's office, which the Maharashtra Governor will attend.
stories.summary: Mumbai commemorates the 18th anniversary of the 26/11 terror attacks on Thursday, with parking banned on several south Mumbai roads from midnight to 10 a.m. Moshe Holtzberg, the child survivor known as 'Baby Moshe', is studying to become a rabbi in New York.
body: Mumbai marks the 18th anniversary of the November 26, 2008 terror attacks on Thursday, with a memorial programme at the Mumbai Police Commissioner's office beginning at 9 a.m. and temporary parking restrictions in force across parts of south Mumbai.

The Mumbai Traffic Police issued a notification on Tuesday barring parking from midnight to 10 a.m. on Thursday. Deputy Commissioner of Police (Traffic, South) Hemrajsingh Rajput said the Maharashtra Governor would attend the programme.

Parking is prohibited on the northbound stretch of Dr. D.N. Road from the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation headquarters to Crawford Market. It is also barred in both directions on Mahapalika Marg and on L.T. Marg between Metro Junction and Badshah Hotel, and at parking lots 1 and 2 of Mahatma Jyotiba Phule Market. Ambulances, police, fire brigade and VIP vehicles and those of other service providers are exempt.

Floral tributes are paid each year at police headquarters, and homage is also offered at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT), Cama and Albless Hospital and other targeted sites, Press Trust of India reported. Residents also gather at "Prerana Sthal", the statue of Assistant Sub-Inspector Tukaram Ombale, who was killed while helping capture the attacker Kasab at Girgaon Chowpatty.

Moshe Holtzberg, the Israeli boy known as 'Baby Moshe', who survived the attack on Nariman House that killed his parents, is now 20 and pursuing rabbinical studies in New York, PTI reported. Rabbi Israel Kozlovsky, who is in charge of Nariman House, said he met Moshe about two weeks ago at a rabbinical conference attended by 4,000 to 5,000 rabbis.
"He is currently pursuing rabbinical studies in New York and wants to become a rabbi. Hopefully, he will return to India. That is our hope," Kozlovsky told PTI.

Moshe's parents, Rabbi Gavriel Holtzberg and Rivka Holtzberg, were killed when the attackers stormed the Chabad House. His nanny, Sandra Samuel, carried him out of the building. He later moved to Israel to live with his grandparents and last visited Nariman House in 2018 with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Nariman House is being renovated and is covered in green safety netting. Kozlovsky said three of its six floors will serve Chabad House activities, while the other three and the ground floor will become a museum and memorial. He said fundraising has begun and construction should finish in a year and a half.
A community prayer has been organised at the Chabad House on Thursday, and Kozlovsky said many delegations are expected.

Mohammed Ajmal Kasab was captured alive and hanged in November 2012. Tahawwur Hussain Rana, another accused in the conspiracy, was extradited from the US in 2025 to stand trial in India.

stories.headline: Telangana women's commission asks Governor to back special probe into egg retrieval racket
stories.dek: The commission also sought a high-level committee and amendments to the Assisted Reproductive Technology Act, citing gaps in how the law is implemented.
stories.summary: The Telangana State Women's Commission met Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla on Wednesday and asked him to recommend a special investigation into an alleged illegal egg retrieval racket in Hyderabad. Police arrested eight people and rescued 43 women on October 31.
body: The Telangana State Women's Commission on Wednesday urged Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla to recommend a special investigation into the network behind an alleged illegal egg (oocyte) retrieval racket in Hyderabad.

Commission Chairperson Nerella Sharada and member Uzma Shakeer met the Governor at Lok Bhavan and briefed him on the findings of the commission's inquiry. The commission also sought a high-level committee to ensure a comprehensive and impartial investigation, according to a release.

Sharada told the Governor that women from different states were allegedly brought to Hyderabad on the promise of jobs and event opportunities, then drawn into illegal egg retrieval by exploiting their financial vulnerability. The commission said it had found that a significant number of women across the country were affected.

"Considering the interstate nature and wider ramifications of the racket, the Women's Commission urged the Governor to recommend a special investigation to uncover the entire network behind these illegal activities," the release said.

The commission also pointed to what it called loopholes and shortcomings in the implementation of the Centre's Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) Act. It asked the Governor to recommend amendments to better protect women's rights, health and safety.

The Governor responded positively and sought detailed information, the commission said. According to the release, he assured the delegation that he would discuss the matter with officials of the departments concerned and consult the state government so that appropriate action is initiated.

Malkajgiri Commissionerate police said they busted the racket on October 31, arresting eight people and rescuing 43 women from four premises in Hyderabad. The women came from Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Maharashtra and other states. Police allege the accused recruited them, brought them to the city and housed them for egg donation procedures at IVF and fertility centres.

The commission has earlier issued notices to eight ART centres and egg banks over suspected irregularities. About 10 days ago, police sought documents from 14 fertility centres, including consent forms and electronic records of egg donation procedures. They want to establish how many women were approached, how often they underwent the procedure and whether the required consent was obtained.

stories.headline: Agreement signed to demolish Kochi's unsafe Chander Kunj Army towers by implosion
stories.dek: The six-month contract with Mumbai-based Edifice Engineering puts the controlled implosion of Towers B and C in early-to-mid April 2027, once all 208 flats are handed over.
stories.summary: Authorities signed an agreement on November 21 with Edifice Engineering to demolish two unsafe 26-storey Army towers at Vyttila, Kochi, by controlled implosion. The blast is expected in early-to-mid April 2027, though no date has been fixed.
body: Authorities signed a formal agreement on November 21 with Mumbai-based Edifice Engineering to demolish the structurally unsafe Chander Kunj Army Towers B and C at Vyttila in Kochi by controlled implosion, with the blast expected in early-to-mid April 2027, Onmanorama reported.

The agreement was signed by Fort Kochi Revenue Divisional Officer G Sai Krishna, for the Army Welfare Housing Organisation (AWHO) and the High Court-appointed Executive Committee headed by the Ernakulam District Collector, and by Shaji Koshy, Edifice's project manager and authorised signatory. It comes about 22 months after the Kerala High Court ordered the demolition.

The contractor will bring down the two 26-storey towers, remove the debris and clear the site up to the pile caps. The schedule provides for 24 weeks of core work, plus 15 days each for mobilisation and demobilisation. The implosion is set for Week 16, which may fall in mid-April. The report said no blast date has been decided and the timeline starts only after all flats are handed over and mobilisation is complete.

Owners of the 208 condemned apartments began handing over keys to AWHO a day before the signing. Edifice sources told Onmanorama that about 80 per cent of the flats had been handed over. A senior official said full-fledged work would start once all flats were handed over.

The net contract value is ₹9,66,40,689, excluding GST, after adjusting an estimated recoverable scrap value of ₹6,25,15,000. A 25 per cent mobilisation advance will be paid against a ₹1-crore bank guarantee. Another 25 per cent will be paid two weeks after the implosion, subject to PWD certification, and the remaining 50 per cent after debris disposal, site handover and statutory compliance certificates.

The first priority is Tower A, where 56 families still live. Edifice must erect 12-foot-high steel barricades, cover the tower with hessian cloth, install two misting systems to control dust and shift the sewage treatment plant, transformers and other utilities. It must also provide temporary parking of at least 56 spaces. Engineering plans are due by December 21, 2026, and the physical work must finish at least a month before the implosion. IIT Madras will assess Tower A's structural safety before and after the demolition.

Because the Kochi Metro viaduct lies about 100 feet and 125 feet from Tower C, according to the logistics plan, Edifice must take out a liability policy of at least ₹75 crore within a month. It needs clearances from PESO, KSEB, Kochi Metro Rail Limited, police, fire authorities and local bodies, and must give two weeks' notice of the blast date. The company is liable for damage to neighbouring structures, utilities and public property.
The official said initial salvaging work could begin in 15 to 20 days.

AWHO built the complex in 2018. It developed serious structural problems, and 208 families, largely serving and retired Army personnel and their relatives, vacated Towers B and C. The Kerala High Court ordered demolition and reconstruction on February 3, 2025, and the Collector formed an executive committee on February 12, 2025.

Edifice was selected on June 1, 2026 after a tender. Rival bidders, including PK Unique Projects, challenged the choice, but the High Court upheld it in September and November 2026.

stories.headline: Maharashtra cabinet approves free foodgrains for 42.3 lakh drought-hit farmers
stories.dek: Farmers in 33 districts who are outside both the food security law and the APL-DBT scheme will get 5 kg per person monthly for three months.
stories.summary: The Maharashtra cabinet on Wednesday approved 5 kg of free foodgrains per person a month for three months for 42.30 lakh farmers in 33 drought-affected districts. Mumbai city, Mumbai suburban and Thane are excluded.
body: The Maharashtra cabinet on Wednesday approved 5 kg of free foodgrains per person each month for three months for 42.30 lakh farmers in 33 drought-affected districts who are not covered by existing food schemes.

The decision was taken at the weekly cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis. Beneficiaries will receive three kg of rice and two kg of wheat per person a month, according to a statement issued after the meeting. Hindustan Times described the recipients as farmers below the poverty line.

Free Press Journal reported that Mumbai city, Mumbai suburban and Thane districts are excluded. The scheme covers farmer families outside the National Food Security Act and the APL Direct Benefit Transfer scheme. The government will review the situation after three months before deciding whether to extend it.

Currently, about 5.79 crore beneficiaries receive free foodgrains under the food security law, while 21.60 lakh farmers in 14 suicide-prone districts get Rs 170 a month under the APL-DBT scheme, the Free Press Journal reported.

Foodgrains will be distributed through e-POS machines after biometric authentication, for ration cardholders whose Aadhaar seeding is complete. The state will seek additional allocation from the Union Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution.

The cabinet also approved Rs 5,548.04 crore for the Narmada-Tapi river-linking project in Nandurbar district. The project is expected to irrigate 26,526 hectares and generate 11.50 MW of electricity, and involves six diversion barrages.

Separately, a cabinet sub-committee on drought led by Revenue Minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule has allowed fodder camps wherever necessary, according to The Times of India. It also made it mandatory to build bridges with embankments to store water, and extended the scheme to give desilted soil free to farmers until June 30.
The state has also sent a proposal to raise rural employment guarantee wages from Rs 317 to Rs 375 to prevent labour migration, the newspaper reported.
keyFacts: 42.30 lakh farmers in 33 districts are covered by the decision.
Each beneficiary gets 3 kg rice and 2 kg wheat monthly.
Mumbai city, Mumbai suburban and Thane are excluded.

stories.headline: ASHA workers stay at Bengaluru's Freedom Park on ninth day of honorarium protest
stories.dek: Chief Minister DK Shivakumar appealed by video call from Japan for an end to the sit-in, but workers want a written assurance on pay.
stories.summary: ASHA workers protesting at Freedom Park in Bengaluru for a ₹15,000 monthly honorarium remained at the site on the ninth day, despite illness and rain. They rejected an appeal from the Chief Minister and said they want a written government assurance.
body: ASHA workers protesting at Freedom Park in Bengaluru for a monthly honorarium of ₹15,000 stayed at the site on Wednesday, the ninth day of their sit-in, after government appeals to end it failed to persuade them.

The workers began the protest on 17 November. According to South First, at least 200 of them have sought medical attention for fever, cough, chills and runny nose after nights in the open, and rain on Tuesday worsened their condition.
Five protesters have been taken to KC General Hospital in the past two days, South First reported. Two had fainted, two had fever, and one complained of shortness of breath and chest pain.

Dr Sujith Kumar, a volunteer doctor at a medical camp on the site, told South First that hundreds had come for medicines and treatment. He said workers had also reported urinary tract infections, fluctuating blood pressure and back pain.

The rain began at 3 pm on Tuesday. Workers first sheltered under the blue tarpaulins they sleep beneath. As it grew heavier in the evening, police helped them move to the parking lot, the outlet reported.

Shobha, an ASHA worker from Mandya district who has spent six days at the park, said she has a headache, runny nose and fever. "I will not go home until the government accepts our demands. There is no alternative; we cannot make a living with the current remuneration," she said.

Chief Minister DK Shivakumar, who is in Japan, spoke to the protesters by video call on Tuesday. "I have special concern for ASHA workers. We will certainly find a solution to your problems. Have faith in me and withdraw the protest," he said.
Shivakumar said he would discuss their demands with the Finance Department during the Assembly session. The workers stood by their demand for a written assurance.
An ASHA worker from Kalaburagi said the government had been willing to pay ₹10,000 last year but had given no concrete assurance on raising the honorarium.

Agriculture Minister PM Narendraswamy drew criticism on Tuesday after saying the government could not give ASHA workers a "gold necklace every time they made a demand". Actor and former Congress MP Divya Spandana, who visited the site, called the remark insensitive and said the government must honour its commitment to pay ₹10,000 a month.
keyFacts: The protest at Freedom Park began on 17 November and entered its ninth day on Wednesday.
Workers demand a monthly honorarium of ₹15,000 and a written government assurance.
Five protesters have been taken to KC General Hospital in two days.
At least 200 workers have sought treatment at the site's medical camp, South First reported.
Chief Minister DK Shivakumar appealed by video call from Japan on Tuesday.

stories.whyItMatters: Hundreds of health workers are sleeping in the open in cold and rain, with some hospitalised, while their pay demand remains unresolved.

stories.headline: Tamil Nadu sets up four-member panel to probe complaint against TVK MLA Arul Vignesh
stories.dek: Police have registered an FIR against the Kallakurichi MLA over a Collector's complaint, and Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin has sought his arrest and a CBI inquiry.
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu government has formed an Internal Complaints Committee, headed by Additional Chief Secretary Kakarla Usha, to inquire into Kallakurichi Collector J E Padmaja's complaint against TVK MLA C Arul Vignesh. He denies the allegations, calling them politically motivated.
body: The Tamil Nadu government has constituted a four-member Internal Complaints Committee, headed by Additional Chief Secretary Kakarla Usha, to inquire into a sexual harassment complaint by Kallakurichi District Collector J E Padmaja against Kallakurichi MLA C Arul Vignesh of the TVK, South First reported on Wednesday.

The committee has 60 days to complete its inquiry and take further action under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013. Usha is the presiding officer. The other members are S Madumathi, IAS; P Sumathi, Secretary of the Law Department; and Sunitha Joe.

Padmaja lodged a formal complaint with District Superintendent of Police Shahnaz I, alleging that Arul Vignesh sent her inappropriate and obscene WhatsApp messages. The complaint also alleges unwanted advances and an attempt to visit her official residence at night.

Police registered an FIR naming the MLA on November 24. The Wire reported that he was booked under Section 75 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which deals with sexual harassment, and Section 132, which covers assault or criminal force to stop a public servant from performing their duty. The Wire's headline said the case followed the Madras High Court pulling up authorities.
The High Court matter arises from a petition by advocate R Thrishuli seeking a direction to register an FIR. Thrishuli had also approached the police seeking action against the MLA.

On Wednesday, Udhayanidhi Stalin, Leader of the Opposition and a DMK leader, submitted a complaint to the Director General of Police seeking Arul Vignesh's immediate arrest and a CBI-led probe. He also sought action against Chief Secretary M Sai Kumar for alleged inaction.

Udhayanidhi said the officer had complained in July and that, instead of acting, the Chief Secretary allegedly asked her to seek a transfer. He said it took 116 days for police to register an FIR. He alleged that the government led by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay had tried to cover up the matter, and said the Opposition no longer trusts it.

His complaint also sought the arrest of Assembly Deputy Speaker M Ravishankar over a separate allegation of assault on a man who had approached him with a complaint. "It has been 16 days since the incident and no action has been taken so far," Udhayanidhi said.

Arul Vignesh has denied the allegations, calling them false and politically motivated. The National Commission for Women has taken suo motu cognisance and sought an impartial inquiry. The government has not been quoted in the available reports on Udhayanidhi's allegations.

She criticised the government's response. Thrishuli's petition seeking an FIR is before the Madras High Court.

stories.headline: Delhi Police say no permission sought for November 26 anti-SIR march
stories.dek: Organisers say they informed police of the Constitution Day march; separately, parties and civil society groups met Delhi's chief electoral officer over voter deletions.
stories.summary: A senior Delhi Police officer said no permission was sought for the November 26 march against the SIR of electoral rolls; organisers say they intimated police. Parties and activists also met Delhi's chief electoral officer over deletions.
body: A senior New Delhi police officer told The Hindu that no permission has been sought for a march against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls planned for November 26. The organisers say they have informed the police.

The Delhi wing of People Against SIR has called a march on Constitution Day from Valmiki Sadan on Mandir Marg to Jantar Mantar. Participants are to assemble at Valmiki Sadan at 12.30 p.m. The organisers have also announced plans to burn copies of the SIR notification.

Maimoona Mollah, a representative of the platform, said an intimation letter was sent to Delhi Police earlier this week. "We make sure not to ask for permission but only inform the police about the march," she said.

Police said "preventive" security measures would be put in place to stop any unauthorised gathering. These include multi-layer barricading, additional personnel and preventive detentions, if required, in view of prohibitory orders.

The march demands the scrapping of SIR, restoration of pre-SIR rolls, no elections on the revised rolls, and restoration of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. It also seeks impeachment and legal action against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and repeal of the 2023 law on the appointment of election commissioners.

The platform claims more than 50% of voters who were on Delhi's rolls in January 2025 and voted in the February 2025 Assembly election have been deleted or marked doubtful. It also alleges 13.3 crore voters have been removed nationwide since the exercise began in Bihar last year. These figures are the platform's claims.

Separately, a delegation of the Aam Aadmi Party, CPI, CPI(M), CPI(ML), activists Anjali Bharadwaj and Amrita Johri, and members of the Voter Adikar Manch met Delhi's chief electoral officer on Monday, according to Hindustan Times.

The delegation said he accepted its suggestions, including restoring deleted voters with their original voter serial and EPIC numbers. For voters deleted and later placed in the ASDD list released on August 31, restoration would be by filling an enumeration form. The delegation said a Standard Operating Procedure would be released shortly.

The group also flagged incorrect Form 7 filings in Mustafabad. It asked that all Form 7 applications be made public, affected voters be notified and decisions follow a hearing. It said cases where an Electoral Registration Officer or assistant filed Form 7 would be re-examined.
An official said the meeting went well. "Several suggestions were already in the pipeline. We will consider all demands which help make the process easier for ordinary voters," the official said.

The delegation's talks centred on a November 6 order giving ASDD-category voters another chance to return to the roll, issued after the Supreme Court's October 28 directions on the SIR.
stories.whyItMatters: Voters deleted during the revision may be able to return to the rolls with original numbers if the proposals are implemented, while the march raises the question of how protests are handled at Jantar Mantar.

stories.headline: BRS and Left leaders detained at Ameerpet protest against Kukatpally truck park auction
stories.dek: Protesters demanded cancellation of the November 27 e-auction by HMDA, which also covers government land in KPHB and Miyapur.
stories.summary: Leaders of the BRS, CPI and CPI(M) were taken into custody on Wednesday during a protest at the HMDA office in Ameerpet against the planned November 27 e-auction of the Kukatpally truck park land. They said public land should not be sold.
body: Leaders of the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) and Left parties were taken into police custody on Wednesday after protesting at the Hyderabad Metropolitan Development Authority (HMDA) office in Ameerpet against a planned November 27 e-auction of the Kukatpally truck park land.

Those detained included Kukatpally MLA Madhavaram Krishna Rao and MLC Shambipur Raju, according to The Hindu. The Times of India reported that the leaders were released later. Leaders of the CPI, CPI(M) and, according to The Hindu, CPI(ML) New Democracy also took part.

The Hindu reported that police barricaded roads leading to the HMDA office in the Swarna Jayanthi Complex and put several activists in preventive custody. Krishna Rao, Raju and Left leaders still reached the building. A scuffle broke out when protesters tried to enter, and they later sat on the main road. The Hindu said traffic between Ameerpet and Maitrivanam was disrupted for over half an hour.

The Times of India said hundreds of truck park beneficiaries, residents of nearby colonies and members of residents' welfare associations gathered near Krishna Rao's office in Kukatpally before moving towards the HMDA headquarters. BRS working president KT Rama Rao condemned the police action.

The auction covers government land in Kukatpally truck park, KPHB and Miyapur. The protesters alleged that land acquired for public purposes was being sold to corporate entities instead of being used for public welfare.

Krishna Rao said farmers and Dalits had voluntarily given up agricultural land for the truck parking facility. He said the park accommodates around 500 trucks. "If these lands are sold, where will the trucks be parked? These lands were acquired for public purposes and must continue to serve the public," he said.

He accused Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy of trying to sell valuable Hyderabad land after taking office. He recalled that in 2005 the government led by then chief minister YS Rajasekhara Reddy tried to sell the truck park land but withdrew the decision after protests by BRS and Left leaders.

BRS leaders said the protest followed a week-long agitation that included hunger strikes and a signature campaign. They said more than 500 heavy vehicles would park at the site every day, and that a sale would push lorries onto the Mumbai National Highway and internal roads in Kukatpally and Balanagar. The Opposition estimates the truck park auction alone could fetch about ₹5,000 crore.

The Opposition has demanded that the land be kept for transport use or turned into parks, hospitals and community halls. Neither report carried a response from the state government or HMDA. The e-auction is scheduled for November 27.

stories.headline: Five Malayalis among 13 killed as bus hits parked truck in Ras Al Khaimah
stories.dek: The bus was returning from Oman after visa renewal procedures; 14 injured passengers are being treated in hospitals, and the Indian Consulate has issued a helpline.
stories.summary: Thirteen people, including at least five Malayalis, died when a bus returning from Oman hit a truck parked on Al Watan Road in Ras Al Khaimah on Tuesday. Four of the Malayali victims have been identified.
body: Thirteen people, including at least five Malayalis, were killed when a bus carrying 41 passengers collided with a parked truck on Al Watan Road in Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates, in the early hours of Tuesday.

Eleven passengers died at the scene and two others died in hospital, according to Onmanorama and South First. Fourteen injured passengers are being treated at hospitals in Ras Al Khaimah. Authorities are expected to release details of the injured.
The bus was returning from Oman after passengers completed visa renewal procedures. The truck had been parked on the roadside following a mechanical failure, the reports said.

Four of the Malayali victims have been identified: Hemanth Puthiyakavil, 29, of Mattannur in Kannur; Ashraf, 53, of Attenganam in Kasaragod; Sangeerthana Suresh, 26, of Thalassery; and Mohammed Ashiq of Kochi. The fifth has not been identified. South First reported that unconfirmed accounts suggest more Malayalis may be among the dead, and that efforts to identify the remaining victims are continuing.

Onmanorama reported that 11 Indians died. Besides the Malayalis, they include Vinod Kumar from Andhra Pradesh, Jignesh from Gujarat and Govindaraj from Tamil Nadu. A Sri Lankan and a Filipino national were also killed.

Sangeerthana was working in Abu Dhabi and had recently secured a new job in Dubai, South First reported. Her relatives said she was due to join the new workplace on Wednesday. Her brother also lives and works in the UAE.

The Indian Consulate said on X it was "deeply saddened by the tragic road accident in Ras Al Khaimah that claimed the lives of several people, including Indian nationals". It shared a 24-hour toll-free helpline, 800-46342, for those seeking assistance.

stories.headline: Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari promises prime-time Bengali film slots after industry meeting
stories.dek: Film industry members also said new theatres will be built at 51 locations and 70 old halls converted, after complaints that Bengali films lose screens to Hindi and English releases.
stories.summary: After meeting film industry members on Tuesday, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari's government promised a prime-time slot for Bengali films in cinema halls. BJP MLA Rudranil Ghosh said 51 new theatres would be built and 70 old halls converted.
body: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari met members of the state's film industry on Tuesday, November 24, and the government committed to a prime-time slot for at least one Bengali film in cinema halls, according to participants.

Actors turned Bharatiya Janata Party MLAs Rudranil Ghosh and Roopa Ganguly were among those present. Ghosh said one Bengali film "will have to be shown during prime time under any circumstances" and that care would be taken to ensure Bengali films are not suddenly removed from shows.

Ghosh said new theatres will be built at 51 locations and 70 old halls will be converted into cinema halls. He said Bengal once had 800 cinema halls and now has around 100. He added that the chief minister had outlined a structured plan asking producers, distributors and other stakeholders to work together.

Ganguly told journalists that many problems were being resolved and that financial approval had been given for many halls. News18, citing ANI, reported that she said the prime-time issue had been addressed and Bengali films would now be shown in that slot.

News18 described the outcome as a directive to cinema halls issued at a meeting with hall owners and producers. The Hindu's account described a meeting with film fraternity members and did not mention hall owners.

Bengali film producer Shrikant Mohta said that if everyone works together on the matters discussed, the Bengali film industry would look completely different five years from now. He said the chief minister had shown commitment and promised several steps.

The meeting followed complaints on Monday, November 23, from the makers of the Bengali film "Sadhak Bamakhyapa", who said they could not secure halls across the state. News18 reported that the film, which is based on the life of a Tantrik, had been dropped from several halls to make way for a new release starring Salman Khan. News18 spells the title "Sadhan Bamakhyapa".

Actor Saheb Chattopadhyay said: "No other regional industry allows this where they push out their own language films to give space to English or Hindi films." He said he was not against films in any language but that regional films should not be displaced.

After the meeting, the BJP's West Bengal social media account said the film would not be sidelined and would be screened across the state. The sources do not say when the prime-time requirement or the theatre plans will take effect.

One Bengali film must be shown in prime time, Rudranil Ghosh said.
New theatres are planned at 51 locations; 70 old halls are to be converted.
Ghosh said Bengal's cinema halls fell from about 800 to around 100.
Makers of "Sadhak Bamakhyapa" had complained on November 23 of losing screens.

stories.whyItMatters: If implemented, the prime-time requirement would affect how cinema halls schedule Bengali films against Hindi and English releases. The theatre plans aim to expand screens in a state where, per Ghosh, halls have declined sharply.

stories.headline: Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy to step down after more than 11 years
stories.dek: The company said a successor will be named in the coming weeks, with Balaji Thiagarajan and the board overseeing operations until then.
stories.summary: Flipkart announced on Wednesday that chief executive Kalyan Krishnamurthy will leave next week, with his last day set for December 4. Walmart declined to say whether the change affects the company's IPO plans.
body: Flipkart announced on Wednesday that chief executive Kalyan Krishnamurthy will step down next week, ending a tenure of more than 11 years at the Bengaluru-headquartered e-commerce company.

A Walmart spokesperson told TechCrunch that his last day will be December 4. Flipkart said it would name a successor in the coming weeks. Until then, Chief Product and Technology Officer Balaji Thiagarajan and the board will oversee operations.

Krishnamurthy joined Flipkart in 2015 from Tiger Global, an early investor, and became CEO in 2017. He remained in the role after Walmart acquired a controlling stake in the company for $16 billion in 2018.

Flipkart said its business grew more than fivefold under his leadership. In its statement, the company pointed to the scaling up of annual sales events such as The Big Billion Days, deeper reach in tier-II and tier-III markets, and new tools for consumers and sellers.

According to TechCrunch, Flipkart has more than 500 million registered users and over 1.4 million sellers, including those on its low-cost platform Shopsy. The report describes it as India's largest online retailer by gross merchandise value, ahead of Amazon. The company has recently moved into quick commerce through Flipkart Minutes and into food delivery through a venture called Eat-in by Minutes.

Chris Nicholas, President and CEO of Walmart International, said: "Both Flipkart and Walmart are better because of Kalyan. We are grateful for his leadership, the governance he instilled and his many contributions to the company."

Krishnamurthy said strong ethics, integrity and governance standards had been central to the company's trajectory. "Our team has helped change how millions of Indians shop, expanding choice and creating opportunities for sellers, entrepreneurs and businesses across the country," he said.
Walmart declined to comment beyond its announcement when asked what prompted the departure and whether it would affect IPO plans. Flipkart did not respond to a request for comment from TechCrunch.

Thiagarajan joined Flipkart in September last year. He previously founded Kasu.ai, a Bay Area startup, and held senior engineering roles at Google, Microsoft and Uber, according to his LinkedIn profile.

stories.headline: Tata Steel CEO says firm is addressing shareholder concerns over APL Apollo deal
stories.dek: APL Apollo shares hit the 15% lower circuit on Wednesday after ICICI Securities, Axis Capital and Nuvama cut their ratings, citing debt and earnings dilution.
stories.summary: Tata Steel CEO T V Narendran said on Wednesday the company is working on shareholder concerns, mainly about debt, over the APL Apollo deal. APL Apollo shares fell 15% to a 52-week low after brokerage downgrades.
body: Tata Steel CEO and Managing Director T V Narendran said on Wednesday that the company is working to address shareholder concerns over its deal with APL Apollo Tubes, as APL Apollo shares fell 15% to their lower circuit and a 52-week low.

Narendran told NDTV Profit that Tata Steel had heard the market's feedback. "We've heard all the noise from the market. We've heard the feedback, both from the Tata Steel shareholders who are more concerned about the debt, and we've addressed a lot of it yesterday in conversations with them," he said.

He said talks were on to find "a solution which addresses all the stakeholders, including shareholders on both sides". APL Apollo Chairman Sanjay Gupta has been in touch with minority shareholders, Narendran said. Internal discussions on whether anything should be done differently had not reached a conclusion, he said.

Asked whether the structure could change, Narendran said the main concern was the debt that would sit on APL Apollo's books after the transaction. The company is looking at "the best way to address it in a manner fair to the APL Apollo shareholders, as well as to the Tata Steel shareholders". He added that independent valuers and one of the top four audit firms were involved in the valuation.
Business Standard reported that since Friday's close APL Apollo has fallen more than 30 per cent to ₹1,478 on the BSE, while Tata Steel has declined over 10 per cent to ₹159.10.

Under the deal, announced on Sunday and Monday, APL Apollo will buy Tata Steel's tubes business and its entire stake in Tata Steel Colors Pvt Ltd for a combined ₹28,000 crore. Tata Steel will acquire the promoters' 26.38% stake at about ₹2,100 per share and make an open offer for a further 26% at ₹2,300 per share. The business transfer requires minority shareholders' approval.

Business Standard put the enlarged APL Apollo's enterprise value at about ₹89,000 crore, including equity value of ₹61,342 crore for the 52.6 per cent stake plus the ₹28,000 crore of debt. APL Apollo will first fund the purchase through acquisition financing and later replace it with long-term capital, including an equity infusion of about ₹18,000 crore, according to Mint.

Three brokerages cut their views on Wednesday. Axis Capital moved to Sell from Buy and cut its target to ₹1,420 from ₹2,400. It called the deal expensive at 24.8 times FY26 EV/EBITDA and estimated FY28 earnings per share could fall 52% to ₹28.

ICICI Securities downgraded the stock to Sell from Add and cut its target to ₹1,345 from ₹2,200, citing higher interest costs from the debt-funded purchase. Nuvama cut it to Hold with a fair value of ₹1,459. The transaction remains subject to approvals.
keyFacts: APL Apollo shares hit the 15% lower circuit on Wednesday, 25 November, touching a 52-week low.
The deal values APL Apollo's purchase of Tata Steel's tubes and colour-coated businesses at ₹28,000 crore.
Tata Steel plans an open offer for 26% of APL Apollo at ₹2,300 per share.

The business transfer needs approval from minority shareholders.

stories.headline: Hera sends first close-ups of crater left in Dimorphos by NASA's DART impact
stories.dek: The European Space Agency spacecraft found the strike flattened one face of the moonlet, left it tumbling in its orbit and freed hundreds of orbiting boulders.
stories.summary: ESA's Hera spacecraft has returned its first close-up images of Dimorphos, showing a stadium-sized crater left by NASA's DART impact in 2022. Scientists said the moonlet is also tumbling and is surrounded by hundreds of boulders.
body: The European Space Agency's Hera spacecraft has released its first close-up images of the asteroid Dimorphos, showing a crater about the size of a sports stadium left by NASA's DART probe, ESA said at an event in Berlin on Wednesday.

The images were presented at the dinosaur hall of the Museum für Naturkunde Berlin, with a livestream starting at 19:45 CET. DART struck Dimorphos, the small moonlet of the larger asteroid Didymos, on September 26, 2022, to test whether an impact could shift an asteroid's path.

Hera principal investigator Patrick Michel of the Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur said scientists had debated whether Dimorphos had gained a crater, changed shape or stayed the same. "Much to our surprise, the answer turns out to be all three at once!" he said in a statement. He said the face struck by DART has been flattened into a crater that extends across the asteroid's entire width.

Michael Kueppers, ESA's Hera mission scientist, said later images showed the impact left Dimorphos "tumbling wildly in its orbit". He said Hera also shows the asteroids are surrounded by hundreds of orbiting boulders, only a few metres in size.
Parts of Dimorphos that DART did not hit appear unchanged. Hera found that the boulder fields there look as they did when DART imaged them in 2022.

Hera launched in October 2024. Scientists already knew the deflection had worked: the orbit of Dimorphos around Didymos was shortened by 33 minutes, according to Space.com. Dimorphos is about 151 m across and Didymos about 730 m, ESA material says.

Hera is now in a rectangular orbit around the pair, holding a distance of about 30 km with its thrusters. It will later move to about 13 km, then deploy two CubeSats. Juventas will probe the interior of Dimorphos with low-frequency radar and attempt to land to measure its gravity. Milani will study dust and materials around the system.

Hera mission manager Ian Carnelli said DART showed an asteroid's orbit can be changed and Hera is revealing what happened to the asteroid itself. Together, he said, the missions are a step towards making deflection "a reliable tool for protecting our planet".
ESA said Hera will move to about 13 km from the asteroids to take more detailed images before the CubeSats are released.
keyFacts: DART hit Dimorphos on September 26, 2022.
Hera launched in October 2024 and now orbits about 30 km from the asteroids.
Hera images show a stadium-sized crater spanning Dimorphos's full width.
Hundreds of boulders, a few metres across, orbit the Didymos pair.
Two CubeSats, Juventas and Milani, will be deployed after Hera moves closer.
stories.background: NASA's DART mission was a test of planetary defence: a spacecraft was deliberately crashed into Dimorphos, which orbits the larger asteroid Didymos. The impact shortened the moonlet's orbit by 33 minutes. Hera was sent to examine the aftermath in detail.
stories.whyItMatters: Hera and its CubeSats are meant to pin down the mass of Dimorphos. Combined with the orbital change, that will help plan future missions to deflect threatening asteroids, according to Space.com.

stories.headline: Calcutta HC defers final hearing on Great Nicobar project as Centre seeks time
stories.dek: The Centre told the court it wants to file another affidavit on tribal rights and renew objections to some petitions; the next hearing is set for January 13, 2027.
stories.summary: The Calcutta High Court deferred the final hearing on petitions against the ₹92,000 crore Great Nicobar Island project on Wednesday after the Centre sought time to file an affidavit and documents. The matter will next be heard on January 13, 2027.
body: The Calcutta High Court on Wednesday, November 25, deferred the final hearing on petitions alleging forest rights violations in the ₹92,000 crore Great Nicobar Island project, after the Centre sought time to file another affidavit and documents on tribal rights.

The bench, led by Chief Justice Ravindra Vithalrao Ghuge, posted the matter for January 13, 2027. On that date the court is also expected to begin hearing a petition challenging orders of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands administration, which said all provisions of the Forest Rights Act (FRA), 2006, were complied with in diverting 121 sq.km. for the project.

The court gave the Centre 10 days to file its affidavits and documents. Petitioners have until the winter break in December to file their rejoinder. The court also agreed to hear Attorney General for India R. Venkatramani's submissions for the government on January 22.

Additional Solicitor General Vikramjit Banerjee told the court that the Centre wished to raise preliminary objections, once again, on whether some of the petitions are maintainable. The final hearing was about to begin under Supreme Court orders when he made the request.

The Centre's lawyers argued that the FRA is not implemented in the islands. They said successive Union governments have held that it need not be pursued there because the Protection of Aboriginal Tribes Regulations, 1956, is already in force.

Petitioners' counsel rebutted this, saying the islands administration had issued a certificate stating that the rights of local tribespeople were settled under the FRA. That certificate is what is being challenged.

The Centre also said it wanted to argue that two more tagged petitions belong before the National Green Tribunal or the Supreme Court. Petitioners' counsel objected, saying those two petitions concern orders reducing the buffer zones of two national parks on Great Nicobar Island.
A decision on the buffer zone petitions will be taken after the winter break.
keyFacts: The Calcutta High Court deferred the final hearing on Wednesday, November 25, 2026.
The Great Nicobar Island project is valued at ₹92,000 crore.
The next hearing is on January 13, 2027; the Attorney General will be heard on January 22.
The Centre has 10 days to file its affidavit; petitioners have until the December winter break to reply.
The project involves diverting 121 sq.km. of forest land.
stories.background: In October, the Centre told the Supreme Court it would be best if the High Court were requested to consider and decide all such cases at the earliest. The Calcutta High Court was to begin the final hearing in line with Supreme Court orders.
stories.whyItMatters: The deferral means the challenges to the forest land diversion, including the tribal rights question, will not be heard on merits until at least January 2027.

stories.headline: California beaches close as record king tides flood low-lying areas
stories.dek: A Nor'easter is forecast to bring damaging winds and up to 75mm of rain to New York City on Thanksgiving, threatening the Macy's parade balloons.
stories.summary: Record or near-record king tides flooded low-lying roads in San Francisco and forced an evacuation in northern California this week. On the East Coast, the National Weather Service issued a high wind warning for New York City ahead of Thursday's Thanksgiving parade.
body: Record-high or near-record November tides flooded low-lying roads in San Francisco and led to the evacuation of one northern California community this week, according to The Guardian, with beaches closed along parts of the coast.

Monthly tide records were set across San Francisco on Tuesday, and some tides were expected to reach higher levels on Wednesday. Residents and local media shared images of water rushing over the Embarcadero, on the bayfront in the city's tourist district, and of flooded roads from San Rafael.

The Guardian reported that forecasts suggest most of California is on track to avoid the worst case, in which coastal flooding is made worse by intense winter rainstorms. Local officials have nonetheless spent weeks preparing for the risk that flooding could disrupt travel in Thanksgiving week, one of the busiest of the year.

On the opposite coast, the BBC reported that a cluster of showers and thunderstorms over the Gulf of Mexico is moving north near the east coast and deepening into a Nor'easter, a storm named for the strong north-easterly winds it drives onto the coast.

The National Weather Service has issued a high wind warning for New York City, Long Island and north-east New Jersey. It takes effect part-way through the Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade and warns of strong to damaging gusts that could affect trees and power lines and cause significant travel disruption.

Winds are forecast to strengthen through Thursday and peak in the evening, so the strongest gusts are likely to arrive after the parade ends. The BBC said there is still a risk that winds could approach the threshold at which the parade's balloons are grounded.

Up to 3in (75mm) of rain could fall, with a flooding risk that could be worsened along the coast as high tides arrive on Thursday evening. Large waves and high sea levels are expected, with a threat of erosion and shoreline damage.
Other eastern parts of the US are also forecast to receive heavy rain and strong winds, with snow in some inland areas adding to Thanksgiving travel problems.
keyFacts: San Francisco set monthly tide records on Tuesday, with higher tides expected on Wednesday.
One community in northern California was evacuated because of tidal flooding.
The National Weather Service issued a high wind warning for New York City, Long Island and north-east New Jersey.
Up to 3in (75mm) of rain could fall in the New York area.
High tides are due on Thursday evening along the north-east coast.
stories.background: King tides are the highest tides of the year, and this week's coincided with Thanksgiving travel. The Nor'easter forming off the US east coast is a separate system from the California flooding.
stories.whyItMatters: Travellers during one of the busiest weeks of the US year face possible road flooding in California and wind, rain and snow disruption in the east.

stories.headline: 27 of 59 rain stations in Kerala cross first drought trigger, KSDMA assessment finds
stories.dek: The state disaster authority has told departments to prepare for reduced water availability this summer after deficits in both the southwest and northeast monsoons.
stories.summary: Kerala's disaster management authority said 27 of 59 rainfall stations with long-term IMD data have reached the 'Trigger-1' drought threshold. The state recorded deficits of 28% in the southwest monsoon and 26% in the northeast monsoon so far.
body: The Kerala State Disaster Management Authority (KSDMA) said 27 of the 59 rainfall monitoring stations for which the India Meteorological Department provided long-term data have reached the 'Trigger-1' threshold, an indicator used to monitor drought, according to a report by The Hindu on November 25.
The 27 stations are spread across 11 districts: Kasaragod, Kannur, Wayanad, Kozhikode, Palakkad, Thrissur, Idukki, Alappuzha, Pathanamthitta, Kollam and Thiruvananthapuram.

During the four-month southwest monsoon, the state received 1,446.4 mm of rain against a normal of 2,001.1 mm, a deficit of 28%. Wayanad had the largest shortfall at 53%, followed by Idukki (46%), Kollam (38%), Alappuzha (32%), and Palakkad and Thrissur (30% each).

The northeast monsoon deficit stands at 26%. Up to November 21, the state received 321.1 mm against a normal of 434.6 mm. Deficits in Ernakulam, Idukki, Kasaragod, Kollam, Malappuram and Thrissur ranged between 30% and 42%.

The assessment said short rain spells separated by long dry periods have limited soil-moisture replenishment and groundwater recharge, leading to poor reservoir inflows. It also cited the influence of the El Niño phenomenon in the Pacific.

A meeting chaired by the State Relief Commissioner directed departments to revive water kiosks and, if needed, use VB-G RAM G workers to set up more. District Collectors were asked to adopt the Kareepra model of quarry pond rejuvenation, used in Kottarakkara, Kollam, for farming and groundwater recharge.
The Water Resources department was told to repair barrage sluice gates promptly to prevent water loss. The Agriculture department will prepare contingency plans at least at block level.

KSDMA Member-Secretary Sekhar Kuriakose told The Hindu that the first round of assessment used rainfall deviation, the Standardised Precipitation Index and dry-spell analysis. The Trigger-2 stage, due by the end of November, will add satellite-based vegetation and water indicators, crop conditions, soil moisture and hydrological data.

Trigger-2 will be followed by field-level ground truthing, which Kuriakose said is essential for districts to access additional funds. The assessment points to the possibility of summer-like conditions setting in as early as the end of January 2027.
keyFacts: 27 of 59 IMD rainfall stations in Kerala have reached the Trigger-1 drought threshold.
Southwest monsoon deficit was 28%: 1,446.4 mm against a normal 2,001.1 mm.
Northeast monsoon deficit was 26% up to November 21: 321.1 mm against 434.6 mm.
Trigger-2 assessment is due to be completed by the end of November.
Wayanad had the worst southwest monsoon deficit, at 53%.
stories.background: Trigger-1 is the first stage of a drought assessment procedure. It is followed by Trigger-2, which uses satellite and hydrological indicators, and then ground verification before districts can access additional funds.
stories.whyItMatters: KSDMA's assessment points to significantly reduced water availability in the coming summer, and departments have been told to prepare water supply, farming and reservoir measures.

stories.headline: Amazon and Meta reportedly hold talks to end block on Muse AI shopping agent
stories.dek: Fortune reports the two companies are negotiating how search results and advertising would work if Muse is allowed to buy from Amazon's store again.
stories.summary: Amazon and Meta have held several rounds of talks on lifting Amazon's two-month block on Meta's Muse AI agent, Fortune reported on Wednesday. Search results and advertising remain unresolved, and any deal would need approval from both chief executives.
body: Amazon and Meta have held multiple rounds of talks about ending Amazon's block on Meta's Muse AI agent, Fortune reported on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the discussions.

Muse is an AI agent, a program that can carry out tasks such as shopping on a user's behalf. About two months ago, Muse users found they could not buy products on Amazon. They received an error message at checkout instead.

According to Fortune, two issues remain under negotiation: how search results would be presented, and how advertising would be handled under any agreement. The Verge, summarising the same report, said the talks also concern the kinds of products the agent recommends and the potential effect on Amazon's advertising revenue.
Fortune reported that any deal would need approval from the chief executives of both companies.

TechCrunch said one of Amazon's biggest concerns is how third-party shopping agents such as Muse could affect its advertising business. Fortune also reported that Amazon executives worry such agents could weaken the company's direct relationship with consumers, according to people familiar with the matter.
In October, Amazon chief executive Andy Jassy argued that few customers were making purchases through outside shopping agents, TechCrunch reported.

TechCrunch also suggested Amazon may have been waiting for Muse to mature before integrating it. If an agent places a wrong order or causes a problem with a purchase, Amazon could be left dealing with unhappy customers and sellers. That point was TechCrunch's own assessment, not an Amazon statement.
Meta and Amazon had not responded to TechCrunch's requests for comment at the time of its report.
keyFacts: Fortune reported the talks on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the discussions.
Muse users have been unable to buy on Amazon for about two months.
Search result presentation and advertising are the open issues, according to Fortune.
Any deal would reportedly need approval from both companies' CEOs.
Meta and Amazon had not commented when TechCrunch published.
stories.background: Amazon blocked Muse from completing purchases roughly two months ago, so users saw an error at checkout. In October, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said few customers were buying through outside shopping agents.
stories.whyItMatters: The outcome would show whether AI shopping agents built by other companies can buy directly from large retailers, and on what terms for search results and advertising.
