stories.headline: MeitY secretary says Sarvam hosting Chinese AI models does not breach IndiaAI scheme
stories.dek: S Krishnan said the Bengaluru startup's access platform is separate from its government-backed work on an indigenous model, and that support for a trillion-parameter model continues.
stories.summary: Electronics and IT Secretary S Krishnan said on Wednesday that Sarvam AI hosting open-source Chinese models does not violate the India AI Mission's principles or misuse government incentives. Sarvam had been criticised after launching a platform offering such models.
body: Electronics and Information Technology Secretary S Krishnan said on Wednesday that Sarvam AI's decision to host Chinese artificial intelligence models does not violate the principles of the India AI Mission.

Krishnan spoke to reporters on the sidelines of the launch of Chariot One, an audio-native AI model developed by Chariot, formerly Gan.ai. He said that hosting open-source, open-weight models, including Sarvam's own, so that AI services can be provided from India, was neither a breach of the mission's principles nor a misuse of the Centre's incentives. Open-weight models are those whose trained parameters are published so others can run them.

Earlier this month, Sarvam said it was launching Token Factory, a platform for running AI models, known as an inference platform, that offers a range of models. These include DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi and Google's Gemma. The first three are Chinese.
The startup was criticised for selling access to Chinese models while also having been selected by the government to build an indigenous model, according to Business Standard.

Krishnan said the development of an indigenous frontier AI model was completely different from Sarvam's offering of access to models. "After all, all AI companies also require revenue and a way in which they can monetise," he said. He added that the government itself uses some of these services internally.

He said Sarvam had used the government's support to produce a 105-billion parameter model and a few others. "In addition, we are continuing to support them as they work towards a trillion-parameter model," he said. Parameters are the internal values a model learns in training, and are a rough measure of its size.
Sarvam, based in Bengaluru, was one of the first startups selected under the ₹10,372 crore India AI Mission to build an indigenous AI model.
keyFacts: S Krishnan, MeitY secretary, spoke on Wednesday at the launch of Chariot One.
Sarvam's Token Factory offers DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi and Google's Gemma models.
Sarvam has built a 105-billion parameter model with government support.
The government says it continues to back Sarvam's work toward a trillion-parameter model.
The India AI Mission has a budget of ₹10,372 crore.
stories.background: Sarvam is among the first startups chosen under the India AI Mission to build an indigenous AI model. Earlier this month it announced Token Factory, which drew criticism because several of its models are Chinese.
stories.whyItMatters: The statement indicates the government does not treat hosting foreign open-weight models as conflicting with funding for domestic AI development, which affects how startups backed by the mission can earn revenue.

stories.headline: 42 US attorneys general oppose Character.ai sale of users' private chats
stories.dek: The states say the chat data of more than 21 million US accounts, including 2.1 million held by minors, should not be sold in the company's bankruptcy.
stories.summary: A coalition of 42 US state attorneys general has intervened in Character.ai's bankruptcy case to block a sale of users' private chat histories. An auction is scheduled for December 1, with one disclosed bidder so far.
body: A coalition of 42 US state and district attorneys general has intervened in the Chapter 11 bankruptcy case of chatbot maker Character.ai to oppose the sale of users' private chat data, according to statements from the officials.
Chapter 11 is a form of US bankruptcy in which a company restructures or sells assets under court supervision. Character.ai filed in October.

The attorneys general said the dataset covers chat histories from more than 21 million US accounts, including more than 2.1 million registered to minors. They said the sale would also include other personal data, such as IP addresses, which identify a device on the internet.

The only bidder disclosed so far is Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC, a Delaware company formed on November 13, 2026, California Attorney General Rob Bonta noted. Character.ai chose it the next day as the base bid for an auction scheduled for December 1. It is unclear what the buyer plans to do with the chats.

The states argue that users would have no protection after a sale. They said a buyer could use or resell the data without disclosure and would not have to honour Character.ai's privacy policy. They also claim the company has given the court less information about possible safety or legal issues than it gave bidders.

Character.ai previously told consumers their personal information would not be sold, the statements noted. In a blog post, the company said users' information would remain protected under its privacy policy.

Some states, including California, Colorado, New York and Connecticut, have chatbot safety laws taking effect on January 1, 2027. The attorneys general said a sale could lead to further violations of those laws.

“Character.AI promised consumers that their data would not be sold. This kind of behavior is illegal under federal and California law and bankruptcy should not be used to sidestep these consumer protections,” Bonta said.

Connecticut Attorney General William Tong said the company's chatbots “drove vulnerable youth down a rabbit hole of emotionally volatile and sexually inappropriate chats”. He urged the bankruptcy court to reject the sale.
keyFacts: 42 attorneys general are opposing the sale in Character.ai's bankruptcy case.
The dataset covers more than 21 million US accounts, over 2.1 million held by minors.
Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC, formed November 13, is the only disclosed bidder.
The auction is scheduled for December 1.
Character.ai filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in October.
stories.background:
A similar but not identical group of attorneys general opposed a proposed $20 million deal giving Disney access to Character.ai's intellectual property, but not users' chats. That deal has not received final court approval, and Disney also agreed to hire most of the company's remaining staff.

Character.ai's co-founders, Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas, returned to Google after it signed a non-exclusive licence to use the startup's technology. The company also faced child-safety lawsuits, including one over the suicide of a 14-year-old Florida boy whose mother said he had become obsessed with a chatbot on the platform.
stories.whyItMatters: The case will help determine whether users' private chatbot conversations can be sold as assets in a bankruptcy despite earlier privacy promises. It affects millions of US account holders, including minors.

stories.headline: Webb telescope finds farthest known 'little red dot', from under 500 million years after Big Bang
stories.dek: The object, CW-LRD-z10, is a strong candidate for the compact, red sources first seen by the telescope, and sits earlier in cosmic history than any previously found.
stories.summary: An international team led by the University of Tokyo's Kavli IPMU has identified the most distant 'little red dot' yet, using James Webb Space Telescope data. The study appears in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.
body: An international team of astronomers has identified the most distant 'little red dot' found so far, using data from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), according to a study in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

The object, named CW-LRD-z10, is described by the researchers as a strong candidate for a little red dot, or LRD. They estimate it existed roughly 400 to 500 million years after the birth of the universe. It is extremely small and shows the characteristic colour of an LRD.

The team was led by Takumi Tanaka, a graduate student at the University of Tokyo's Kavli Institute for the Physics and Mathematics of the Universe (Kavli IPMU), and included professor John Silverman. They analysed high-resolution infrared images from JWST's COSMOS-Web large-scale observation programme.

Finding such an object was difficult. JWST's near-infrared instruments cover wavelengths between 0.6 and 5 µm, but light from very distant objects has been stretched to longer wavelengths by the expansion of the universe. The team developed a method that combines data from two JWST instruments, NIRCam (near-infrared) and MIRI (mid-infrared).

The researchers then checked the distance with spectroscopic observations. The spectrum showed a Lyman-alpha break, caused by absorption by neutral hydrogen, along with emission lines from hydrogen, carbon, nitrogen, oxygen and iron. It also resembled the spectra of previously found LRDs. The study title gives the object's spectroscopic redshift as 10.36.

Until now, the only LRDs found had existed between 600 million and 1.5 billion years after the Big Bang. Some theories suggest that black holes that were precursors to supermassive black holes may have formed about 500 million years after the Big Bang.
The team said the number density of LRDs it determined was consistent with predictions for how their abundance changes over cosmic time, proposed in earlier studies.

Next, the researchers plan to study CW-LRD-z10 in more detail through its hydrogen emission lines, which reveal black hole activity, and through the distribution of its light. They also aim to find other LRDs from a similar period to establish when LRDs first appeared and how they formed.
keyFacts: CW-LRD-z10 is the most distant little red dot found so far, the study says.
It is estimated to date from about 400 to 500 million years after the Big Bang.
Earlier LRDs found existed between 600 million and 1.5 billion years after the Big Bang.
The team combined JWST NIRCam and MIRI data and confirmed distance by spectroscopy.
The study is led by Takumi Tanaka of Kavli IPMU, University of Tokyo.
stories.background: Little red dots, faint objects thought to involve supermassive black holes, were first detected in the early universe by JWST in 2022. Supermassive black holes have been detected when the universe was 700 to 800 million years old, and how they formed so quickly remains an open question in astronomy.
stories.whyItMatters: Because LRDs may hold clues to how supermassive black holes formed so early, an object from before 500 million years after the Big Bang gives researchers a new data point for testing theories on those origins.

stories.headline: South Pole Telescope team releases sharpest map yet of matter in distant universe
stories.dek: Scientists from 30 institutions mapped mass by measuring how gravity bent the oldest light in the universe, using 2019 and 2020 observations.
stories.summary: A collaboration of scientists from 30 institutions has released what it calls the sharpest map yet of mass in the universe, built from South Pole Telescope data. The map tracks how gravity bent the cosmic microwave background.
body: A group of scientists from 30 institutions has released what it describes as the sharpest and clearest map yet of mass in the universe, made from South Pole Telescope data and posted to the arXiv preprint server.

The map is based on the cosmic microwave background (CMB), the earliest light in the universe, which has travelled for more than 14 billion years. Gravity from galaxies and galaxy clusters bends that light slightly. By cataloguing this effect, known as gravitational lensing, researchers can reconstruct the matter lying between Earth and the point where the light was emitted.

The telescope is run by a collaboration led by the University of Chicago and sits at the NSF Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station. The US Department of Energy's Argonne National Laboratory is the lead DOE laboratory for its operations. The analysis used 2019 and 2020 observations covering about 1,500 square degrees of sky.

"This is the deepest map of the universe we have so far—it's like taking a photograph with very low background noise exposure," said Yuuki Omori, a University of Chicago research scientist and lead author of the paper.

The map is the most sensitive measurement of CMB gravitational lensing to date, according to the report. It allows tests of how "clumpy" the universe is, meaning how matter is lumped together. That indicates how structure grew over time, including the middle period when stars and galaxies began forming in earnest. Combined with Dark Energy Survey data, the new results are the best yet at narrowing down how that structure formed, the report said.

Wei Quan, an Argonne postdoctoral appointee and co-author, led the conversion of raw sensor data into a microwave image of the sky. The team then measured the lensing in each part of the image and built the mass map. It checked its methods against simulated images that included CMB signals and realistic noise. Quan said this helps ensure the map reflects matter in the universe rather than instrument effects or foreground signals.

The results agree closely with other CMB experiments, including the Planck satellite and the Atacama Cosmology Telescope in Chile. The data can also be compared with measurements of baryon acoustic oscillations, which track the universe's expansion.

Amy Bender, an Argonne physicist and co-author, said the measurement offers a view that complements studies of galaxies and galaxy clusters. John Carlstrom, the SPT project director, said: "We are entering the new era of cosmology promised by these instruments."

The team hopes such data could eventually yield insights into neutrinos, whose combined mass leaves an imprint on how structure grows. It also sees the work as progress toward detecting primordial gravitational waves, ripples from the Big Bang that could offer a measurement of cosmic inflation.
keyFacts: Scientists from 30 institutions released the map, posted to the arXiv preprint server.
The map uses South Pole Telescope observations from 2019 and 2020.
The data cover about 1,500 square degrees of sky.
Results agree with the Planck satellite and the Atacama Cosmology Telescope.
Combined with Dark Energy Survey data, the results best narrow how cosmic structure formed.
stories.background: The cosmic microwave background is sometimes called the afterglow of the Big Bang. Gravitational lensing slightly bends its light as it passes galaxies and galaxy clusters, letting researchers infer the distribution of matter, including matter that emits no light.
stories.whyItMatters: The map gives cosmologists a way to test models of how the universe's structure grew and to cross-check other surveys. The team also sees it as a step toward studying neutrinos and primordial gravitational waves.

stories.headline: Gukesh draws game 2 against Sindarov with London System after 20 moves
stories.dek: The World Championship match in Geneva stays level at 1-1 after both players repeated moves; Gukesh later called the opening a "cool" way to start.
stories.summary: D Gukesh drew the second game of the World Chess Championship with Javokhir Sindarov on Wednesday, repeating moves after 20 with the white pieces. Gukesh defended his choice of the London System, and the third game is on Thursday.
body: World champion D Gukesh drew the second game of the World Chess Championship against Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov on Wednesday, playing the London System with white and agreeing a three-fold repetition after 20 moves in Geneva.
The score is 1-1 in the 14-game match. Game 1 on Tuesday, which began with the Berlin Defence, also ended in a draw by repetition, after 38 moves.

Wednesday's game was played at the library of Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny. It was Gukesh's first game with white in the match. He opened with d4, Sindarov answered with d5, and Gukesh developed his dark-squared bishop to f4.

Sportstar reported that Sindarov again held a clock advantage. Gukesh took a long time before his 16th move, a pawn push to f3, and fell more than half an hour behind. From move 16 the players shuffled their pieces, with Gukesh's bishop moving between e5 and g3, until the position repeated.
Sportstar also noted that Sindarov claimed the draw correctly this time. In game 1, the arbiter had told him his claim was premature.

Speaking afterwards, Gukesh defended the opening. "Nowadays everything from both colours is playable, there is so much to explore because of the engines, I don't think one opening is better than the other, I thought it would be a cool way to start," he said, according to PTI.

Gukesh said neither player could gain an advantage because "both are well prepared". Explaining why he did not play on, he said: "I could not see a way to pose some serious problems for my opponent, and if I have to take some measures, I also have to take a certain amount of risk."
Sindarov said he had not expected the opening but knew the variation. He said both sides had solid positions and progress was not easy in the early middle game.

Gukesh said he felt fine and energetic, noting that only two of the 14 games had been played. He said he would reveal details of his team's composition later. His Polish second, Grzegorz Gajewski, and friends Shikhar and Charmie are with him in Geneva.
The third game is on Thursday.
keyFacts: Game 2 ended in a draw by three-fold repetition after 20 moves on Wednesday.
The match is level at 1-1 in a 14-game contest.
Gukesh played white and chose the London System.
Game 1, a Berlin Defence, lasted 38 moves before a repetition draw.
Game 3 is scheduled for Thursday.
stories.background: Ding Liren, whom Gukesh succeeded as world champion, played the London System twice in the 2024 title match in Singapore, according to Sportstar. Both of those games were drawn. Gukesh and Sindarov are both 20 years old, and Sportstar describes the match as the youngest World title match in history.

stories.headline: IPL 2027 auction register lists 1,220 players, 281 of them overseas
stories.dek: The 10 franchises will now tell the league which players they want in the final pool, which will be released on Friday, December 4.
stories.summary: A total of 1,220 players, 939 Indian and 281 overseas, are on the register for the IPL 2027 auction. The auction will take place on Wednesday, December 16, with the final list due on December 4.
body: A total of 1,220 players have been named in the register for the IPL 2027 auction, made up of 939 Indian players and 281 overseas players from 17 countries, according to Sportstar.
The register has 184 capped players, 994 uncapped players and 42 players from Associate Nations. Of the uncapped players, 925 are Indians, and 127 of them have played in earlier IPL seasons.

The 14 capped Indians on the list are Akash Deep (base price Rs. 1 crore), Avesh Khan (Rs. 2 crore), Deepak Chahar (Rs. 2 crore), Deepak Hooda (Rs. 75 lakh), Jaydev Unadkat (Rs. 1 crore), Karun Nair (Rs. 75 lakh) and Kuldeep Sen (Rs. 75 lakh).

The others are Mayank Agarwal (Rs. 75 lakh), Rahul Tripathi (Rs. 75 lakh), Saransh Jain (Rs. 75 lakh), Shivam Mavi (Rs. 75 lakh), Tushar Deshpande (Rs. 1 crore), Umesh Yadav (Rs. 1 crore) and Umran Malik (Rs. 75 lakh).

Australia has the most overseas players with 53, followed by South Africa (40), West Indies (36), New Zealand (25) and Afghanistan (23). Among Associate Nations, USA has the most with 13, ahead of UAE and Nepal with 10 each.

The 10 franchises will fill the remaining 66 slots. They must now inform the league which players they want included in the final player pool. The final auction list, along with the player sets, will be released on Friday, December 4. The auction will be held on Wednesday, December 16.

stories.headline: Ackerman and Mulder hit centuries as South Africa reach 494 for 7 against Bangladesh
stories.dek: South Africa lead by 403 runs at Centurion after a second day of 406 runs, while Bangladesh's Shoriful Islam said the pace attack lacked discipline.
stories.summary: Marques Ackerman made 150 and Wiaan Mulder 100 as South Africa finished the second day of the second Test at 494 for 7, 403 runs ahead of Bangladesh. Shoriful Islam said Bangladesh's bowlers had been too short and too wide.
body: Marques Ackerman scored 150 and Wiaan Mulder 100 as South Africa ended the second day of the second Test against Bangladesh at Centurion on 494 for 7, a lead of 403 runs over the visitors' first-innings 91.

South Africa added 406 runs in 98 overs on the day. Ackerman, who began on 46 not out, reached his second hundred in successive Tests off 111 balls and became the fastest South African to 150, doing so in 137 balls. He scored 104 runs in the morning session and was out lbw to a full toss from Shoriful after a review failed.

Every South African batter made at least 20. Tony de Zorzi, in his first Test in a year, made his fourth Test fifty off 104 balls before edging Taskin Ahmed to wicketkeeper Jaker Ali. Marco Jansen, at No. 8, hit 67 off his seventh Test fifty, including a six off Mominul Haque into the stadium burger joint.

Mulder reached his fifth Test century off 177 balls, from the first ball of the last over. He fell to the next ball he faced, edging Towhid Hridoy to Jaker for Hridoy's first Test wicket. Jansen is 33 runs short of a maiden Test hundred, and Cricinfo said South Africa showed no sign of declaring.

Bangladesh picked four specialist pace bowlers for the first time in 23 years and left out spinner Mehidy Hasan Miraz, the first time since 2003 they have played a Test without a specialist spinner. The four pace bowlers sent down 79 overs and conceded 333 runs for six wickets. Part-timers Mominul, Hridoy and captain Najmul Hossain Shanto bowled 36 overs between them.

Shoriful finished with 2 for 95 from 21 overs. Khaled Ahmed took 2 for 88. "I admit that we didn't bowl well enough," Shoriful said. "I think we bowled boundary balls at the start and end of overs." He added that the bowlers had been too wide and too often back of a length, and that "almost everyone made the same errors".
Bangladesh also lost wicketkeeper Litton Das to a groin problem in the 67th over. Jaker took the gloves, and it is not known whether Litton will be cleared to bat.
keyFacts: South Africa finished the second day on 494 for 7, leading by 403 runs.
Marques Ackerman made 150 off 137 balls, the fastest 150 by a South African.
Wiaan Mulder scored his fifth Test hundred, 100 off 177 balls.
Marco Jansen is 33 not out short of a maiden Test hundred, on 67.
Litton Das left the field with a groin problem in the 67th over.

stories.whyItMatters: South Africa hold a 403-run lead, leaving Bangladesh needing to bat for long periods, possibly without Litton Das, to avoid defeat.

stories.headline: FIA finds Williams exceeded 2025 F1 cost cap by £627,000
stories.dek: Alpine were also found in breach of the rules, though the FIA said theirs was a procedural failing and not an overspend; both teams signed settlement agreements.
stories.summary: The FIA found Williams exceeded Formula 1's 2025 cost cap by £627,000, which the team said was unintentional. Williams face a financial penalty and a 1.5% cut in aerodynamic research time, while Alpine were found to have made a procedural breach.
body: Formula 1's governing body, the FIA, has found that Williams broke the sport's cost cap during the 2025 season, exceeding the limit by £627,000. The team said the overspend was unintentional.
The cap last season was $135m (£106m). The FIA said Williams' breach was equivalent to a 0.48% overspend, which it said "falls at the lower end of the less than 5% minor overspend range".

Williams and Alpine have each reached an 'accepted breach agreement' with the FIA. Williams' agreement includes a financial penalty, the amount of which has not been disclosed, and a 1.5% reduction in permitted aerodynamic research and development time for the next 12 months. Both teams must also pay the costs of the FIA's investigations.

Williams said the breach related to administrative costs incurred in changing its company structure. "We believed these costs fell outside of the cap. Following discussions with the FIA, we have agreed to resolve the matter in line with their interpretation that the costs should have been in cap," the team said in a statement.
The team added that the FIA had noted Williams gained no sporting or financial advantage and acted co-operatively and in good faith during the review.

The FIA said in its own statement: "There is no accusation or evidence that (Williams) sought at any time to act in bad faith, dishonestly or in a fraudulent manner, nor that it wilfully concealed any information from the cost-cap administration." It said the financial regulations are complex and the breaches arose from an interpretation adopted in good faith.

Alpine were found to have committed a procedural breach without overspending, and have also been given an undisclosed financial penalty. The team said it "unknowingly committed a procedural breach" because of inaccuracies in its full-year reporting documentation on costs related to exclusions and adjustments.

Alpine said the errors involved non-sporting and operational costs that the cost cap administration recognised gave no performance advantage. It listed marketing, non-F1 activities, HR activities, employee bonus costs, offsetting of costs and inventory costs.

Williams finished fifth in the constructors' championship in 2025. They are ninth this season with two races remaining, after targeting the 2026 regulations as a chance to move back towards the front.
keyFacts: Williams exceeded the 2025 cost cap by £627,000, equal to a 0.48% overspend.
The 2025 cap was $135m (£106m).
Williams lose 1.5% of permitted aerodynamic research time for 12 months.
Alpine committed a procedural breach without overspending; both teams face undisclosed fines.
Williams are ninth in the constructors' standings with two races left.
stories.background: Formula 1 teams are limited in how much they can spend each season under a cost cap enforced by the FIA. Breaches of less than 5% are classed as minor overspends, and teams can settle them through accepted breach agreements.
stories.whyItMatters: The settlements set financial and technical penalties for both teams, including a reduced aerodynamic development allowance for Williams over the next 12 months.

stories.headline: Ramayana: Part One nears ₹1,000 crore in India as day 21 haul falls to ₹7.37 crore
stories.dek: Pinkvilla's trade estimates put the Ranbir Kapoor-Yash film at about ₹1,700 crore worldwide, ahead of Dhurandhar: The Revenge, though its Hindi-belt run has fallen short of expectations.
stories.summary: Ramayana: Part One earned ₹7.37 crore net in India on its third Wednesday, its lowest day so far, taking its total to ₹980.32 crore, according to Sacnilk. Pinkvilla estimates a worldwide gross of about ₹1,700 crore, a record for an Indian film's original release.
body: Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana: Part One collected ₹7.37 crore net in India on day 21, its weakest single day since release, taking its India net total to ₹980.32 crore, according to figures from Sacnilk cited by Hindustan Times.
The Wednesday number was less than half of the ₹17.50 crore the film earned on Tuesday, per the same report. The film ran across 14,886 shows. Sacnilk puts its India gross at ₹1,170.85 crore.

Pinkvilla's trade estimates differ from Sacnilk's. It reported ₹16.50 crore on the third Tuesday, a 40 per cent rise on Monday, which it attributed to affordable ticket pricing and a holiday. It put the 20-day India net at ₹938.75 crore, including 3D charges. That is ₹716.25 crore from Hindi and ₹222.50 crore from dubbed versions. Excluding 3D charges, it gave ₹878.00 crore.

Pinkvilla also estimated the film's worldwide gross at ₹1,700 crore as of Tuesday, ahead of the ₹1,679 crore for Dhurandhar: The Revenge. It split this into ₹1,129 crore from India and ₹571 crore (USD 60.75 million) overseas. On that basis, it ranks Ramayana first among Indian films in original release.

Dangal remains the highest-grossing Indian film of all time at ₹1,910 crore, including ₹1,125 crore from China, Pinkvilla said. Ramayana is due to release in China, Japan, Korea, Taiwan and Russia next year. Pinkvilla said those markets could supply the ₹50-60 crore needed to pass Dangal.

The outlet projected a finish near ₹1,850 crore worldwide. It said the film had underperformed in the Hindi and Telugu markets, and that the Hindi heartland had not delivered the expected jump. Pinkvilla said its figures are subjective trade estimates, not audited collections.

Ramayana, titled Ramayana: Rise of a Legend overseas, is the first of two films. Ranbir Kapoor plays Rama, Sai Pallavi plays Sita and Yash plays Ravana. The film has also reached the top 20 contenders in the visual effects category for the 99th Academy Awards, Hindustan Times reported, citing Variety. It is on two Critics Choice shortlists, for visual effects and stunt design.

stories.background: Ramayana: Part One is the first of a two-film adaptation of the Hindu epic, directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash. Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman composed the music, and DNEG and ReDefine handled visual effects.

stories.headline: Avengers: Doomsday crosses ₹50 crore in India advance sales, 22 days before release
stories.dek: Premium seats in Mumbai are priced at ₹3,000 to ₹4,000, and some cinemas have scheduled shows from 12.05am, according to Hindustan Times.
stories.summary: Marvel's Avengers: Doomsday has passed ₹50 crore in advance sales in India with 22 days to go, Pinkvilla reported. Hindustan Times said premium Mumbai tickets are going for up to ₹4,000, while Dune: Part Three also draws interest.
body: Marvel's Avengers: Doomsday crossed ₹50 crore in advance bookings in India at the end of business on Monday, 22 days before its December 17 release, according to entertainment site Pinkvilla.

Pinkvilla said only six Hollywood films have earned more than ₹50 crore in advance sales in India, making Doomsday the seventh. It said the film is on sale on about 500 screens. Opening-day sales of around ₹20 crore a week ago set the pace, and the release of the final trailer on Monday night added momentum, the site said.

Hindustan Times reported a lower figure, saying the film had reportedly earned over ₹41 crore in pre-sales, with around 6.55 lakh tickets sold across 6,700 shows at an average price of ₹640. The two reports do not explain the gap, and both describe the numbers as trade estimates or reported figures.
Ticket prices vary widely by city and format. Hindustan Times said tickets in Delhi-NCR start at ₹520, with recliners going up to ₹2,000. In Mumbai, premium seats are selling for ₹3,000 to ₹4,000.
Some cinemas have scheduled shows from 12.05am, and a few in Mumbai have screenings at 3.30am and 6.30am, the newspaper said.

Trade analyst Atul Mohan told Hindustan Times: "The most expensive ticket ever sold in Mumbai, as far as I can recall, has been for Avengers: Doomsday, around ₹4,000." He added: "This current advance is proof that fans don't care about money when there's a film they really want to watch."

Pinkvilla said the current Hollywood advance-sales record, held by Avengers: Endgame and Spider-Man: Brand New Day, stands at over ₹120 crore. It put the overall record at probably over ₹150 crore, held by Dhurandhar: The Revenge or Pushpa: The Rule. The site said Doomsday could target ₹200 crore.
Its "Pinkvilla Predicts" forecast puts the film's opening day at ₹95-105 crore nett. Pinkvilla said its figures are subjective trade estimates, not certified collections.

Hindustan Times said Dune: Part Three, which stars Robert Pattinson, Timothee Chalamet, Zendaya and Jason Momoa, is also drawing advance interest, particularly for premium formats such as IMAX. It releases on December 18.

stories.headline: Nollywood actor Pete Edochie dies in Enugu aged 79
stories.dek: The Things Fall Apart star, known for his deep voice and use of proverbs, had prostate cancer, his family said in a statement.
stories.summary: Nigerian actor Pete Edochie, one of Nollywood's best-known faces, died in Enugu on Wednesday aged 79, his family said. He had been ill with prostate cancer, and tributes have come from fans, fellow actors and the Enugu governor.
body: Nigerian actor Pete Edochie, one of Africa's best-known film stars, died aged 79 in the early hours of Wednesday in Enugu, in south-eastern Nigeria, his family announced.

The family said in a statement that he died after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. A statement shared on Instagram by his son Leo said: "As we mourn this painful loss, we pray that Almighty God grants his gentle soul eternal rest and gives the entire family the fortitude to bear this irreparable loss."

Edochie began his career as a broadcaster in 1967 before moving into acting. He came to wider attention in 1987 in a television adaptation of Chinua Achebe's novel Things Fall Apart, playing Okonkwo, the Igbo warrior at the centre of the story. BBC News reported that the role brought him international recognition.

He went on to become one of the most recognisable faces of Nollywood, Nigeria's film industry. He often played traditional rulers, wealthy businessmen and family patriarchs, and was known for his deep voice and his use of African proverbs.

His films included Igodo, Rituals, Billionaire's Club and the 2018 romantic comedy Lionheart. In 2003 he received the national honour Member of the Order of the Niger (MON). He also won the Industry Merit Award at the Africa Magic Viewers' Choice Awards.
In recent years, his facial expressions, remarks and scenes from his films reached a younger audience through viral social media memes.

Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah said the death was a huge loss to Nigeria. He praised Edochie for introducing international audiences to Igbo traditions and for inspiring younger performers. "Pete Edochie was more than an accomplished actor, he was an institution," Mbah said.
Abubakar Yakubu, president of the Actors Guild of Nigeria, called Edochie a "father figure" in the entertainment industry and said his influence would be felt for generations.
Edochie had spoken publicly about his health during a visit to Ghana in October, saying he was struggling to walk and had swelling in parts of his body.
He is survived by his wife, Josephine, and their six children, among them the Nollywood actors Yul and Linc Edochie.
keyFacts: Pete Edochie died aged 79 on Wednesday in Enugu, Nigeria.
His family said the cause was a prolonged battle with prostate cancer.
He rose to prominence in 1987 as Okonkwo in a Things Fall Apart adaptation.
He received the Member of the Order of the Niger in 2003.
He is survived by his wife Josephine and six children.
stories.background: Nollywood is Nigeria's film industry, which BBC News says has grown into one of the world's largest. Edochie's career began in broadcasting in 1967, and he later appeared in numerous films over several decades.

stories.headline: Top Gear to return in 2028 with Gordon Ramsay as host
stories.dek: The BBC motoring show has been off air since Andrew Flintoff's on-set crash in 2022, and will film across the UK and abroad in 2027.
stories.summary: The BBC confirmed on Wednesday that Top Gear will return in 2028 with chef Gordon Ramsay as host. The show has been off air since a 2022 crash involving co-host Andrew Flintoff.
body: The BBC confirmed on Wednesday that Top Gear will return to its screens in 2028, with chef and entrepreneur Gordon Ramsay as host, according to The Hollywood Reporter.

The new series will be produced by BBC Studios Entertainment Productions for BBC One and BBC iPlayer. The broadcaster said Ramsay would set the agenda and lead a new lineup of co-presenters through "epic adventures, daring tests and spectacular stunts". The co-presenters have not been named in the source report.

Filming will take place across the UK and around the world in 2027. The Top Gear Test Track at Dunsfold Aerodrome in Surrey will again serve as the show's home and base. The Stig, the show's racing driver, will also return.

The programme has been off air since 2022, when co-host Andrew Flintoff was involved in a crash on the test track. He suffered serious facial and rib injuries when his open-top vehicle overturned. The show was previously presented by Jeremy Clarkson, James May and Richard Hammond.

Ramsay has appeared on Top Gear as a guest three times: in the first series in 2002, the eighth in 2006 and the 23rd in 2017. His fastest lap, one minute 46.3 seconds in a Chevrolet Lacetti, placed him seventh on the show's "Star In A Reasonably Priced Car" leaderboard.

"My love affair with cars began as a child, growing up a field away from Silverstone, where I would climb over the fences and sneak in for a glimpse of the racing," Ramsay said. He added that the aim was to build on the show's spirit of the unexpected, "bringing a fresh energy and ambition to create something truly thrilling for a whole new generation of audiences".

The series was commissioned by Ed Havard, the BBC's director of entertainment, and Michael Jochnowitz, head of constructed reality and studio entertainment. Mel Balac is creative director for BBC Studios, Rowland French is showrunner and Zac Assemakis is executive producer.

stories.headline: Bhanushali Studios sues Aanand L Rai's Colour Yellow in Bombay High Court
stories.dek: Amazon MGM Studios, AVS Studios Private Limited and Amazon Seller Services Private Limited are also named as respondents; the nature of the dispute has not been disclosed.
stories.summary: Vinod Bhanushali's Bhanushali Studios Limited has filed a commercial suit in the Bombay High Court against Aanand L Rai's Colour Yellow Media Entertainment. The matter is listed for December 1, and neither side has said what the dispute is about.
body: Vinod Bhanushali's Bhanushali Studios Limited has filed a commercial suit in the Bombay High Court against Colour Yellow Media Entertainment Pvt. Ltd., the production company of filmmaker Aanand L Rai, Bollywood Hungama reported on Wednesday.

According to case details the outlet accessed, the suit was filed on October 12, 2026, and registered on November 19, 2026. Amazon MGM Studios, AVS Studios Private Limited and Amazon Seller Services Private Limited are also named as respondents.
The matter is at the pre-admission stage and is listed for hearing on December 1, 2026.

The reporting does not say what the dispute concerns. Bollywood Hungama said industry insiders believe Amazon's presence among the respondents could point to a link with Nayyi Navelli, a Yami Gautam-starrer produced by Colour Yellow and Amazon. The outlet noted that Bhanushali was credited under 'Special Thanks' in the film. It said it was not clear whether the case relates to the film or to some other commercial arrangement between the parties.
Bhanushali confirmed the suit when Bollywood Hungama contacted him. "The case is subjudice. All I can say is that yes, I have indeed moved court against Aanand L Rai," he said.
Rai declined to comment, the outlet reported. There was no response from Amazon in the source material.
The December 1 hearing is the next scheduled step in the case.
keyFacts: Bhanushali Studios Limited is the plaintiff in a commercial suit at the Bombay High Court.
The suit was filed on October 12, 2026, and registered on November 19, 2026.

stories.headline: KMF cuts Nandini curd price by ₹2 a kg from November 29
stories.dek: The federation acted about 20 days after Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar directed a reduction following complaints from hoteliers and consumers over the November 1 increase.
stories.summary: The Karnataka Milk Federation will lower the price of Nandini curd by ₹2 per kg from November 29. A 500-gram packet will cost ₹33 and a 1-kg pouch ₹66.
body: The Karnataka Milk Federation (KMF) has announced a reduction of ₹2 per kg in the selling price of Nandini curd, effective November 29, nearly 20 days after Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar directed it to do so, The Hindu reported.
Under the revised rates, a 500-gram packet, now priced at ₹34, will sell for ₹33. A 1-kg pouch, now ₹68, will cost ₹66.

An official KMF release said the prices of Nandini milk and curd were revised from November 1, 2026, following a request from the state's milk producers. It said the Government of Karnataka then directed KMF to reduce the curd price "in the interest of consumers".

The increase drew criticism from hoteliers, the general public and others. The Bangalore Hotels Association and the Karnataka State Hotels Association wrote to the Chief Minister asking him to bring down curd prices, which had risen by more than ₹8.
In the previous month, a 500-gram packet of curd cost ₹28 and a 1-kg pouch cost ₹54. The reduction announced for November 29 applies only to curd, according to the KMF release.
keyFacts: The new curd prices take effect on November 29.
A 500-gram packet falls from ₹34 to ₹33.
A 1-kg pouch falls from ₹68 to ₹66.
The November 1 revision followed a request from milk producers, KMF said.
Last month a 500-gram packet cost ₹28 and a 1-kg pouch ₹54.

stories.headline: CMRL floats tenders to finish entry and exit works at Phase II elevated stations
stories.dek: The agency says the work includes pending repairs and escalator and lift access at stations that opened on the Yellow Line in October.
stories.summary: Chennai Metro Rail Limited has floated tenders to complete balance architectural works, including entry and exit facilities, at newly opened Phase II elevated stations. It has also pushed back morning Yellow Line services by an hour to allow construction and testing.
body: Chennai Metro Rail Limited (CMRL) has floated tenders to complete the remaining architectural works, including entry and exit facilities, at the newly opened elevated stations under Phase II, according to a report published on November 25.

The works also cover pending repairs and infrastructure needs meant to improve passenger convenience. CMRL said the remaining work would be taken up at the newly operational stations so that all passenger facilities are completed.

At some stations, entry and exit work, including escalators and lifts, is still pending. CMRL said this would be addressed promptly. The agency also said it would carry out inspections to identify issues and respond to demands raised by commuters.

The tenders follow the start of passenger services in October on the Yellow Line between Poonamallee Bypass and Porur Junction, which connects Vadapalani. Trains are running on the stretch, but certain architectural and related works at the stations are incomplete.
Separately, CMRL has temporarily revised morning timings on the Yellow Line from Tuesday. Services between Poonamallee Bypass and Porur Junction now start at 7 am instead of 6 am.

The revised schedule is meant to allow construction and testing at the remaining seven stations in the Porur Junction–Vadapalani section. The longer block hours will also let CMRL speed up testing of the Automatic Signalling System needed for Unattended Train Operations (UTO).
CMRL said the changes were necessary to speed up commissioning and improve connectivity along the stretch. It acknowledged the inconvenience to passengers.
keyFacts: CMRL has floated tenders for balance architectural works at newly opened Phase II elevated stations.
Pending entry and exit work, including escalators and lifts, is to be completed at some stations.
Yellow Line services between Poonamallee Bypass and Porur Junction began in October.
Morning services on that stretch now start at 7 am instead of 6 am, from Tuesday.
Seven stations in the Porur Junction–Vadapalani section remain to be completed and tested.

stories.headline: Delhi's major hospitals record 6,581 lung cancer cases in six and a half years
stories.dek: Replies to RTI applications show 913 deaths across four institutions, about one every three days, though Safdarjung Hospital did not share its case count.
stories.summary: Four of Delhi's prominent government hospitals reported 913 lung cancer deaths between January 2020 and July 2026, according to RTI replies obtained by PTI Bhasha. Three of them recorded 6,581 cases, about 83 a month.
body: Three prominent government hospitals in Delhi recorded 6,581 lung cancer cases between January 1, 2020, and July 31, 2026, an average of 83 a month, according to replies to Right to Information applications filed by PTI Bhasha.

Across four hospitals, 913 patients with lung cancer died in the period, which works out to one death every three days. The institutions are AIIMS, RML Hospital, Safdarjung Hospital and the Delhi State Cancer Institute (DSCI).
Safdarjung Hospital gave only its death toll, 393, and did not disclose its number of cases. The 6,581 figure therefore covers the other three hospitals.
AIIMS recorded the most cases. For the period from January 2020 to March 2026, it reported 4,860 cases and 158 deaths, or about 65 cases and two deaths a month.

DSCI reported 1,613 cases and 354 deaths between January 1, 2020, and July 2026, about 20 cases and four deaths a month. It said two children were diagnosed in 2021 and that 351 women had lung cancer over the period. It did not break down deaths by gender.
RML Hospital reported 108 cases, including 47 women, and eight deaths.
The applicants also sought data on patients who had never smoked. None of the institutions provided it.

A senior DSCI doctor, who spoke to PTI on condition of anonymity, said the institute receives patients from Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Bihar and Nepal as well as Delhi. The doctor said the primary cause of lung cancer is smoking or exposure to tobacco smoke, with genetic mutations also playing a role.

Doctors said lung cancer has also been found in women who do not smoke, and that this is suspected to be linked to genetic mutations and pollution. They said the disease is often diagnosed only in its final stages, which makes treatment extremely difficult.

Dr Geeta Kadayaprath of the Apollo Athenaa Women's Cancer Centre said long-term exposure to polluted air can raise the risk of lung cancer. She noted that the International Agency for Research on Cancer, part of the World Health Organization, has classified outdoor air pollution and its particulate matter as carcinogenic to humans. PM 2.5 particles are small enough to penetrate deep into the lungs, she said.

Dr Vikas Maurya of Fortis Hospital in Shalimar Bagh said early stages often show no clear symptoms. Possible warning signs include a persistent cough, coughing up blood, shortness of breath, chest pain, voice changes, unexplained weight loss and recurring chest infections. A standard X-ray cannot detect the condition, he said; a CT scan is required.
keyFacts: 6,581 lung cancer cases were recorded at AIIMS, DSCI and RML between January 2020 and July 2026.
913 lung cancer deaths were reported across four hospitals, including Safdarjung.
AIIMS reported 4,860 cases and 158 deaths from January 2020 to March 2026.
DSCI reported 1,613 cases and 354 deaths; Safdarjung reported 393 deaths.
No hospital provided data on lung cancer patients who had never smoked.
stories.background: November is observed as Lung Cancer Awareness Month, and Delhi is currently dealing with severe air pollution. Health experts say long-term exposure to polluted air raises lung cancer risk but is not the only cause; smoking and genetic mutations are others.
stories.whyItMatters: Doctors say lung cancer is often found only at a late stage, when treatment is hardest, and that early symptoms can be absent. The hospitals' lack of data on non-smokers leaves that question unanswered.

stories.headline: Andhra Pradesh says Telangana plans to draw 2 tmc ft daily from Nagarjunasagar
stories.dek: The Andhra Pradesh government says its Palnadu drinking water grid needs 1.865 tmc ft a year, far less than Telangana's Sunkishala project could take.
stories.summary: Andhra Pradesh has alleged that Telangana's Sunkishala project would let it draw two tmc ft of Krishna water a day from Nagarjunasagar. Andhra says its own Palnadu Water Grid needs 1.865 tmc ft annually; neither state has drawn water yet.
body: Andhra Pradesh has alleged that Telangana plans to draw two tmc ft of Krishna water a day from the Nagarjunasagar reservoir through its Sunkishala drinking water project, while its own Palnadu Water Grid needs 1.865 tmc ft a year.

The Andhra government raised concerns over the gap in the proposed quantities. It said Telangana's project could allow water to be drawn even during prolonged dry spells, according to Deccan Chronicle. The Wire reported that the Palnadu project has revived the competing claims of the two states over Krishna waters.

Andhra Pradesh said the previous BRS government in Telangana planned the Sunkishala project and built an intake well about 200 metres long, 50 metres wide and 70 metres deep. Its three tunnels were set at different levels, the lowest at 134 metres, against the reservoir's dead storage level of 155.45 metres. Andhra alleged this violates norms.

Nearly 100 tmc ft of water lies below the dead storage level, in a reservoir with a total capacity of 312 tmc ft. Andhra said the intake would let Telangana draw water even if the level fell during long periods without rain in the catchment area. Sunkishala was due for completion in 2024 but was delayed after a wall of the intake well collapsed.

Andhra's Palnadu project is to supply drinking water to 33 mandals in Palnadu district and other areas through pipelines. The previous Telugu Desam government under N. Chandrababu Naidu initiated it in 2014, but it made little progress because of a lack of funds and the change of government in 2019. After the present government took office in 2024, it proposed water grids in five districts: Prakasam, Palnadu, East Godavari, West Godavari and Chittoor.

An agency had been finalised by March 2025 under GO-56, issued on February 16, 2022. The project was first estimated at 1,200 crore, shared equally by the Centre and the state under the revamped Jal Jeevan Mission, and needed 0.3 tmc ft for 10 mandals. Expansion to 33 mandals raises the annual requirement to 1.865 tmc ft for 30 years, up to 2057, at an additional cost of 2,000 crore.

Andhra has begun building an intake well near the reservoir in Palnadu district, with three vents, the lowest at about 150 metres. That is 21 metres above Telangana's lowest tunnel. The state alleges the difference would let Telangana draw more water through the year.

A government official in Andhra Pradesh said: "The quantum of water proposed to be drawn from Nagarjunasagar reservoir through the Palnadu Water Grid project is less than the quantum that gets wasted in evaporation and leaks at the irrigation projects in any given time."
Both states are building their projects, and neither has drawn water from the reservoir so far. The sources provided did not include a response from Telangana.
keyFacts: Andhra Pradesh alleges Telangana plans to draw two tmc ft daily from Nagarjunasagar.
Palnadu Water Grid needs 1.865 tmc ft annually for 33 mandals, up to 2057.
Sunkishala's lowest tunnel is at 134 metres; dead storage level is 155.45 metres.
Andhra's intake vent is at about 150 metres.
Neither state has drawn water from the reservoir so far.
stories.background: Nagarjunasagar has a total capacity of 312 tmc ft. Telangana's Sunkishala project, planned by the previous BRS government, was due for completion in 2024 but was delayed after an intake well wall collapsed. Andhra Pradesh's Palnadu grid was first initiated in 2014 and expanded from 10 to 33 mandals.
stories.whyItMatters: The dispute concerns drinking water supply to 33 mandals in Palnadu district and other areas of Andhra Pradesh, and how Krishna water in Nagarjunasagar is shared between the two states.

stories.headline: Vigilance files first chargesheet against Vellappally Natesan in microfinance case
stories.dek: The Kollam Vigilance Court received the filing after the Kerala High Court ruled that prior government sanction is not needed under the Prevention of Corruption Act.
stories.summary: The Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau filed its first chargesheet against SNDP Yogam general secretary Vellappally Natesan and others in the microfinance fraud case. The filing followed a High Court order that no prior government sanction was required.
body: The Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) filed its first chargesheet in the microfinance fraud case before the Kollam Vigilance Court on Wednesday, naming Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana Yogam (SNDP Yogam) general secretary Vellappally Natesan, president M.N. Soman and other accused.
Vigilance SP S. Sasidharan, who heads the special investigation team, appeared in person to submit the document, The Hindu reported.

The filing followed an interim order by Kerala High Court Judge Justice A. Badharudeen. The judge held that prior government prosecution sanction is not required to file a chargesheet under the Prevention of Corruption Act. He directed the agency to file the chargesheet against Mr. Natesan on or before November 26.
According to the report, the Vigilance department had been unable to file a chargesheet for ten years because the State government withheld prosecution sanction.

The case concerns allegations that between 2003 and 2014 the accused took loans worth crores of rupees at low interest from the Kerala State Backward Classes Development Corporation under a microfinance scheme. They are alleged to have diverted about ₹15.85 crore in government funds by submitting utilisation certificates in the names of bogus self-help groups and lending the money at high interest rates.
Vigilance registered the case in 2016, naming Mr. Natesan as the prime accused, on a complaint from former Chief Minister V.S. Achuthanandan.

As the investigation dragged on, M.S. Anil, a native of Cherthala, approached the High Court seeking to speed up the probe. The court then began monitoring the case directly. Mr. Sasidharan later conducted a detailed inquiry and prepared around eight chargesheets, according to The Hindu. The report did not say whether the others have been filed.
keyFacts: VACB filed the first chargesheet before the Kollam Vigilance Court on Wednesday.
Accused include Vellappally Natesan and SNDP Yogam president M.N. Soman.
Alleged diversion of government funds is about ₹15.85 crore.
The case was registered in 2016 on V.S. Achuthanandan's complaint.
Justice A. Badharudeen ruled prior government sanction is not required.
stories.background: The allegations relate to loans taken between 2003 and 2014 from the Kerala State Backward Classes Development Corporation under a microfinance scheme. Vigilance said the case was held up for a decade because the State government did not grant prosecution sanction, until the High Court, acting on a petition by M.S. Anil, began monitoring the probe.
stories.whyItMatters: The filing lets the trial process begin against the leadership of SNDP Yogam in a case that has been pending since 2016.

stories.headline: 73 of 110 complaints against major BMC hospitals pending on MARG portal
stories.dek: HBT Medical College and Dr RN Cooper Hospital have the most unresolved grievances, at 21, while LTMG Hospital in Sion has closed none of its 16.
stories.summary: Seven months after the BMC launched its MARG grievance portal, 73 of 110 complaints against its major hospitals, or 66.4%, remain pending, according to hospital-wise data. Peripheral and special hospitals show lower pendency.
body: Nearly two-thirds of complaints registered against major hospitals run by the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) remain unresolved, with 73 of 110 grievances (66.4%) pending, according to hospital-wise data from the MARG portal.
Only 37 of the 110 complaints against major hospitals have been closed. The Free Press Journal reported on the data on Wednesday.

HBT Medical College and Dr RN Cooper Hospital has the most pending complaints, at 21 out of 51 received. Lokmanya Tilak Municipal General Hospital (LTMG) in Sion has 16 pending out of 16 received, with none recorded as closed. Nair Hospital Dental College has five pending complaints, while KEM Hospital and BYL Nair Charitable Hospital have one each.

Peripheral hospitals fared better. Of 114 complaints received, 96 were closed and 18 remain pending, a pendency rate of 15.8%. M W Desai Hospital has the most pending in this category at six, followed by Rajawadi Hospital with three.
Special hospitals recorded two pending complaints out of 16 received, a pendency rate of 12.5%. Both pending complaints are at Kasturba Hospital for Infectious Diseases.
Of the 240 grievances recorded across the three categories, 104 (43.3%) were marked invalid. The data did not say why they were classified that way.
Officials said the main complaints concerned shortages of medicines, non-functional diagnostic equipment, delays in treatment, staff shortages, overcrowding and poor sanitation.
For the health department as a whole, the portal shows 565 complaints, of which 229 are closed, 288 are pending and 175 are termed invalid.
Calls and messages to Prajakta Lavangare-Verma, Additional Municipal Commissioner (City), seeking her response on the pending health grievances went unanswered.
keyFacts: 73 of 110 complaints against major BMC hospitals are pending, a rate of 66.4%.
LTMG Hospital, Sion, has 16 pending out of 16 received, none closed.
Peripheral hospitals have a pendency rate of 15.8%; special hospitals, 12.5%.
104 of 240 hospital complaints, or 43.3%, were marked invalid.
MARG portal was launched on April 22, 2026.
stories.background: The BMC launched the MARG (Management and Redressal of Grievances) portal on April 22, 2026, with Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde inaugurating it. It centralises complaints received through the BMC website, the 1916 helpline, the MyBMC app and a WhatsApp chatbot. It provides for time-bound resolution and escalation of unresolved complaints to senior officials.
stories.whyItMatters: Patients at the BMC's major hospitals, where most complaints are pending, have had fewer grievances resolved through the portal than those at peripheral or special hospitals.
